As for Ishmael and his children, and his brothers and Esau, the Lord did not bring them near to Him; although they are the children of Abraham, He did not choose them.

A people shall be His, for He has chosen Israel. Many nations and many peoples are His, for all belong to Him, and all shall be subject to Him, gathering together from all the children of men. Yet, after Him, He has made them to be a multitude above all.

But over Israel, He alone is their chief; whether an angel or a spirit, He has not made any to be above them. He shall keep them. From the hand of angels and spirits, from all authorities, He shall protect them, and He shall guide them. They shall be His children, and from this day forth, even unto eternity, He shall be their God, and He shall bless them.

Now, the children of Israel, I tell you this law, as they are likely to act deceitfully. They shall not be able to conceal their children from their bodies; for the children of Belhor shall all be born as they are, and they shall not be able to conceal them.

For He has broken His covenant, and His word has departed; this strong covenant shall be established among the children of Israel. This sign shall not be fulfilled, lest they perish from the earth; their bodies have been made as nations, and they have acted foolishly and have stumbled.
In this land, for the sins committed, all iniquity shall be utterly removed, so that henceforth, there shall be no place for sin, and they shall have no forgiveness.

In the fourth month, in the time of the harvest, it was revealed to Abraham beneath the oak; and we spoke with him. As it is given to him from his wife Sarah, so it is; for Sarah has heard this matter spoken with Abraham, and she laughed. And we also have been given; and she, having heard this matter, laughed as it was spoken.
And the name of her son shall be called Isaac, as it was decreed in heaven, as it was written. And at that time, when we returned to her, she bore a son.

And in that month, the Lord executed judgment upon Gomorrah and upon Sodom, upon all the cities of the plain and upon the Jordan region. He consumed them with fire and brimstone; for they were exceedingly wicked and sinful, and their bodies were as if they were being consumed, as they wrought iniquity upon the earth. Behold, all their works He destroyed, even unto this day.
Likewise, the Lord shall execute judgment upon all the places wherein they have wrought iniquity, as He did unto Sodom.

And the Lord remembered Abraham, and delivered Lot; He brought him forth from the midst of the destruction. From the time of Adam until this day, He hath wrought no sin upon the earth that was not done with his children; for a father hath slept with his son.

He shall destroy them and shall awaken them; He shall execute upon them a judgment like unto that of Sodom, that in the day of judgment no seed of man may remain upon the earth. Behold, it is commanded. And upon all His children, a decree was established in heaven.
And in that month, Abraham journeyed from Hebron and dwelt between Kadesh and Sur, in the mountains of Gerar.
In the fifth month, he also journeyed and dwelt by the well of Lahai-roi.

And in the sixth month, the Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and the Lord did unto Sarah as He had spoken. For Sarah conceived and bore a son. And in the third month, on the same day of the month, the Lord said unto Abraham, "At this time will I return unto thee, and Sarah shall have a son."
And Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day, as God had commanded him; and he was named according to the covenant that was established before the foundation of the world.
In the fourth year, in the sixth month, we came unto Abraham and unto the middle of the valley. And as we returned unto her, it was revealed unto Sarah as it had been spoken; and she also bore a son.

In the seventh month, we returned; and Sarah also found joy before us, for Sarah had borne a son. And the Lord blessed Sarah, saying, "You shall not die until you have borne seven sons, and until you have reached the fullness of life as it has been commanded unto you."
And by the name of Isaac shall he be called. And his children shall be a multitude; and they shall be counted among the nations.
And one of the children of Isaac shall be a holy seed; and he shall be a great blessing, and he shall not be counted among the nations.
And his seed shall be separated from all the people, to be a glorious people unto the Lord, for the kingdom and the priesthood, and to be a holy people unto Him, as He shall look upon them, the God.
And we walked in our way; and all that was spoken was concerning Sarah; and both were exceedingly joyful in their unity.
And for the one who was cast out, in the land where he was exiled, he rejoiced in the Lord, and there he built an altar unto the Lord.
And in this month, at the middle of the valley, on the seventh day, a feast of joy was made.
በዚህችም በዓል ለእርሱና ለአገልጋዮቹ ዳስ ሠራ፤ እርሱም አስቀድሞ በምድር የዳስ በዓልን አደረገ።
በዚህም በሰባቱ ቀን ሁልቀን በየዕለቱ ሁለት ላሞች፥ ሁለት የበግ ሙክቶችና ሰባት በጎች፥ ስለ ኀጢአትም አንድ የፍየል ጠቦት፥ ስለ ልጆቹና ስለ እርሱ ያስተሰርይበት ዘንድ ለእግዚአብሔር የሚቃጠል መሥዋዕት በመሠዊያው ላይ ያቀርብ ነበር።
ለድኅነት መሥዋዕትም ሰባት የበግ ሙክት፥ ሰባት የፍየል ጠቦት፥ ሰባት በጎች፥ ሰባት የፍየል ሙክት አቀረበ። መሥዋዕታቸውንና ወይናቸውንም በስባቸው ሁሉ ላይ አቀረበ። ለበጎ መዓዛም የተመረጠ ዕጣንን በመሠዊያው ላይ ጥዋት ጥዋት ያጥን ነበር።
በሰርክም ሽቱን ያጥን ነበር። ነጭ ዕጣንን፥ ቀንዓትን፥ ልባንጃን፥ ናርዶስን፥ ከርቤና ሰንቡልን፥ ቀበርቾንም እነዚህን ሰባቱን ሁሉ ያጥን ነበር፤ የተወቀጠውንና የተመረጠውን፥ የተስተካከለውንና የተቀላቀለውን፥ ንጹሑንም ያቀርብ ነበር።
እርሱም በፍጹም ልቡ፥ በፍጹም ነፍሱም ደስ እያለው በቤቱ ካሉት ሁሉ ጋር ሰባት ቀን ይህን በዓል አደረገ፤ ከእርሱም ጋር ባዕድ ወይም ያልተገረዘ ሰው ማንም አልነበረም።
ለዘለዓለም ትውልድ የጽድቅ ተክል ከእርሱ እንደሚሆን ስላወቀና ስለ ተረዳ ለፈቃዱ ፈጥሮታልና የፈጠረውን አምላኩን አመሰገነው። ሁሉን እንዳደረገ እንደ እርሱም ይሆን ዘንድ ከእርሱ ቅዱስ ዘር ይሆናል።
ይህችንም በዐል ባረካት፥ ደስም አለው፤ ስምዋንም የእግዚአብሔር በዓል ብሎ ጠራት። ልዑል አምላክም ደስ ብሎት የሚቀበላት የእግዚአብሔር በዓል አላት።
ለዘለዓለም ባረክነው፤ ከእርሱ በኋላም ዘሩን ሁሉ እንደ ሰማይ ጽላት ምስክር ያቺን በዓል በጊዜዋ አድርጎአልና በምድር ትውልድ ሁሉ ባረክነው።
ስለዚህም በዘመናትና በዓመታት ሁሉ በትውልዳቸው የዘለዓለም ሕግ ሊሆን በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ተቀባይነት ያለው የዳስ በዓልን በደስታ ሰባት ቀን የሚያደርጉ ይሆኑ ዘንድ ለእስራኤል በሰማይ ጽላት ተጻፈ።
በዓሉን ያደርጉት ዘንድ፥ በጥላም ይቀመጡ ዘንድ፥ በራሳቸውም አክሊል ይደፉ ዘንድ፥ ከወንዙም የአኻያውን ቅጠል ቅርንጫፍ ይይዙ ዘንድ፥ በእስራኤል የዘለዓለም ሥርዐት ሆኖ ተጽፎአልና ለዚህ ሥርዐት የተወሰነ ዘመን የለውም።
አብርሃምም ለጋውን የሰሌን ጫፍ፥ ያማረ የእንጨቱንም ፍሬ ይዞ በየቀኑ በዘንባባው ሰባት ጊዜ መሠዊያውን ይዞር ነበር።
ጥዋት ጥዋትም ሁሉን የፈጠረ አምላኩን በደስታ ያመሰግን ነበር።
በዚህ ኢዮቤልዩ በአምስተኛው ሱባዔ በአንደኛው ዓመት ይስሐቅ ጡት ጣለ።
አብርሃምም ልጁ ይስሐቅ ጡት በጣለባት ቀን በሦስተኛው ወር ታላቅ በዓል አደረገ። የግብፃዊቷ የአጋር ልጅ ይስማኤልም በአባቱ በአብርሃም ፊት በቦታው ተቀምጦ ነበር።
አብርሃምም ደስ አለው። ሁለቱን ልጆቹን አይቶአልና፥ ልጅንም ሳይወልድ አልሞተምና።
ሎጥ ከእርሱ በተለየባት ቀን የተናገረውንም ነገር አሰበ። ምድርን ይወርሳት ዘንድ በምድር እግዚአብሔር ዘርን ሰጥቶታልና ደስ አለው። የሁሉን ፈጣሪም በአፉ አመሰገነው።
ሳራም ይስማኤልን ሲጫወትና ሲዘፍን አየችው፤ አብርሃምንም እጅግ ደስ ብሎት አየች። ይስማኤልንም ባየችው ጊዜ ቀንታ አብርሃምን፥ “የዚህች የባሪያ ልጅ ከልጄ ከይስሐቅ ጋር ርስት አይወርስምና ይህችን ባሪያ ከልጅዋ ጋር አስወጥተህ ስደዳት” አለችው።
ከእርሱ ለይቶ ይሰዳቸው ዘንድ ስለ ባሪያውና ስለ ልጁ በአብርሃም ፊት ኀዘን ሆነ።
እግዚአብሔርም አብርሃምን፥ “ስለ ሕፃኑና ስለ ብላቴናዪቱ በፊትህ ኀዘን አይሁን፥ በይስሐቅ ስምና ዘር ይጠራልሃልና፥ ሳራ የነገረችህን ነገር ሁሉ ስማና አድርግ። ስለዚያች ባሪያ ልጅ ግን አትዘን፤ ከልጆችህ ወገን ነውና ታላቅ ወገን አደርገዋለሁ” አለው።
አብርሃምም በጥዋት ገሥግሦ ሄዶ ውኃ ያለበትን ረዋትና ዳቦውን አምጥቶ ለአጋር አሸከማት፤ ልጁንም አሳዝሎ ሸኛት፤ በቤርሳቤህ ምድረ በዳም እየተቅበዘበዘች ሄደች።

And the water had departed from her; and her son was thirsty; and she went and sat down over against him, a good way off, as it were a bowshot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
And one of the holy angels said unto her, “Why dost thou weep? The Lord hath heard thy voice, and the child shall not perish; arise, take the child in thine hand.”
And her eyes were opened, and she saw a well of water; and she filled the bottle with water, and gave the child drink; and she arose and went into the wilderness of Paran.

And the child grew, and was strong; and the Lord was with him. And his mother took him a wife from the daughters of Egypt; and she bare him a son. And she said, “In the time of my trouble, the Lord hath been near unto me,” and she called his name a prophet.

In this jubilee, in the seventh sabbath, in the first year, in the first month, it came to pass. On the twelfth day of this month, the Lord, as He desired, spoke concerning Abraham, and His words were heard in heaven; and in all that was spoken, it was as if it were believed, for in all his afflictions, he was indeed steadfast.
And the guardian stood before God and said, “Behold, Abraham loves his son Isaac; he delights in him more than all others; let him bring an offering upon the altar.”

“If you do this, you shall see; in all that you fear, he is indeed steadfast.” But the Lord knew that Abraham was steadfast in all his afflictions; for in his land, he was beset by famine; and among the kings, he was beset by wealth; and he was also beset by his wife’s position; and he was beset by his own struggles; and in the time of their departure, he was beset by his son Ishmael and by his servant Hagar; in all the trials he encountered, he was found steadfast, and his body did not falter.
For he is steadfast, and he loves the Lord; his work he does not forsake.

And the Lord called unto Abraham, saying, “Abraham, Abraham, Abraham,” and Abraham answered, “Here I am.” And He said, “Take now your beloved son Isaac and go to the mountain that I shall show you; and there, as I speak to you, offer him upon one of the mountains.”

And then he rose early in the morning; he saddled his donkey, and took with him two of his young men, and his son Isaac; and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up and went to the place which God had told him.

And he saw the place afar off; and he came to the place where the water was, and he said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey; I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and we will return to you.”
And he took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it upon his son Isaac; and he took the fire in his hand and the knife, and they both went together to that place in unity.
And Isaac spoke unto his father, saying, “My father,” and he answered, “Here I am, my son.” And he said, “Behold the fire and the wood; but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”

And he said, “My son, God will provide for Himself the lamb for the burnt offering.” And they came to the place which God had told him; and he built an altar there and laid the wood in order; and he bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar upon the wood. And he reached out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.
እኔም በፊቱ ቆምሁ ፤ በመኰንን መስቴማም ፊት ቆምሁ።
እግዚአብሔርም፥ “እርሱ እግዚአብሔርን የሚፈራ እንደ ሆነ ዐውቄአለሁና በይስሐቅ ላይ እጁን እንዳያወርድ፥ በእርሱም ምንም ክፉ ነገር እንዳያደርግ ንገረው” አለ።
በሰማይም ሆኜ፥ “አብርሃም፥ አብርሃም” ብዬ ጠራሁት። እርሱም ደንግጦ፥ “እነሆ፥ እኔ አለሁ” አለኝ። “በሕፃኑ ላይ እጅህን አታውርድ፤ አንተ እግዚአብሔርን የምትፈራ እንደ ሆንህ ዛሬ ዐውቄአለሁና፤ ከእኔም ለበኵር ልጅህ አልራራህምና በእርሱ ላይ ምንም አታድርግ” አልሁት፤ መኰንን መስቴማም አፈረ።
አብርሃምም ዐይኖቹን አቅንቶ አየ። እነሆ፥ ቀንዱን በዕፀ ሳቤቅ የተያዘ አንድ በግ ሲወርድለት አየ። አብርሃምም ሄዶ ያን የበግ አውራ አምጥቶ ስለ ልጁ ፋንታ ለሚቃጠል መሥዋዕት አቀረበው።
አብርሃምም ያን ቦታ፥ “እግዚአብሔርን ያየሁበት” ይባል ዘንድ፥ “እግዚአብሔር የታየበት ቦታ” አለው፤ ተራራውም ደብረ ጽዮን ነው።
እግዚአብሔርም አብርሃምን በሰማይ ሆኖ ዳግመኛ በስሙ ጠራው፤ በእግዚአብሔር ስም እንነግረው ዘንድ እንደ ታየነው፤ እግዚአብሔር “በራሴ ማልሁ አለ” አልነው።
“ይህን ነገር አድርገሃልና፥ ለምትወድደው ለበኵር ልጅህ ከእኔ አልራራህለትምና ፈጽሜ እንድባርክህ፥ በባሕር ዳር እንዳለ አሸዋና እንደ ሰማይ ኮከብ ዘርህን ፈጽሜ እንዳበዛው፥
ልጆችህም የጠላቶቻቸውን ሀገር እንዲወርሱ፥ ቃሌን ስለ ሰማህ ፋንታ በዚህ ዓለም ያሉ አሕዛብንም ሁሉ እንዲወርሱ እኔ ባዘዝሁህ ሁሉ አንተ ለእኔ የታመንህ እንደ ሆንህ ለሁሉ ነገርሁ፤ በሰላም ሂድ” አለው።
አብርሃምም ወደ ብላቴኖቹ ሄደ። ከዚያም ተነሥተው በአንድነት ወደ ቤርሳቤህ ሄዱ። አብርሃምም በመሐላ የውኃ ጕድጓድ አደረ። ያችንም በዓል በሄደባቸውና በሰላም በተመላለሰባቸው በሰባቱ ቀኖች መጠን በዘመኑ ሁሉ ሰባት ቀን የደስታ በዓል አደረጋት። የእግዚአብሔርም በዓል አላት።
ሰባት ቀን በደስታ ይህችን በዓል ለማድረግ በልጆቹና በእስራኤል ላይ እንደ ታዘዘ በሰማይ ጽላት እንዲህ ተሠርቶአል፤ ተጽፎአልም።
In the forty-second jubilee, in the first week, in the first year, Abraham returned and dwelt beside Hebron for two years of the jubilee. This is the city of Kiryat Arba.
In this jubilee, in the third week, in the first year, the life season of Sarah was fulfilled; and she died in Hebron.

And Abraham went to mourn for her, and his heart was grieved. And he spoke not a word, as it was in his heart. And thus, he mourned for her, and he found a place to bury her, and he spoke with the children of Heth in his heart and did not act hastily.

And the Lord gave him favor in the sight of all the people, and he spoke to the children of Heth, saying, "Give me a possession for a burial site." This is also Hebron. And he purchased it for four hundred shekels of silver.
And they said, "We will give it to you without cost," but he gave them the full price of the place, and he did not accept anything from them, and he bowed to them.

After this, he buried her in the cave of Machpelah. And Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years; these were the years of her life. And these are two jubilee periods and one year. This is the day of the years of Sarah's life.

And Abraham, being tested, and his heart being grieved, this trial was tenfold; for him, it was given, and after him, it was given to his son. The Lord did not forget what He spoke concerning Canaan; and there he buried her, to have a place for the dead. He was found to be faithful and grieved, and in heaven, he was written as a friend of God.
In the fourth year, he took a wife for his son Isaac, and her name was Rebekah; she is the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and the sister of Laban.

And Abraham, after the death of Sarah, took a third wife from among his children born in his house; her name was Keturah. And she bore him six children: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
In the second week of the second jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, Rebekah bore two sons to Isaac, Jacob and Esau.
And Jacob was a perfect man, but Esau was a man of the field, a hunter; and Jacob dwelt in tents. These were the generations.
Jacob learned to write; but Esau was a man of the field and a skillful hunter, and he did not learn. He became skilled in robbery and all evil deeds. Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.
Abraham saw the deeds of Esau, but he knew that by the name of Jacob and his son he would be called.
And Rebekah called and said, "Rather than love Esau, let Jacob be loved." And she commanded concerning Jacob's matter.

"My son, keep Jacob, my son; for he shall be a blessing among the children of men because of me; and he shall be a guide for the seed; and among all the people who dwell upon the earth, may the Lord choose him."
Behold, my son Isaac loves Esau more than Jacob; but I cannot allow you to go out and love Jacob; and moreover, to do anything for him is beyond my ability.

From today until the end of the world, he shall be a blessing upon the earth, and your eyes shall be toward the beloved. I have loved him more than all my children, and I have chosen him for the everlasting honor, and his seed shall fill the earth. Let your hands be strong. Let your heart rejoice in your son Jacob; for a man may count the fish of the sea, and so shall his seed be counted.

May the Lord bless me and my seed with all the blessings of this age for Jacob and his seed; and may his name be honored among his seed; the names of the fathers, of Shem and of Noah, of Enoch and of Melchizedek, of Methuselah and of Seth and of Adam shall be blessed; for they shall be for the foundation of heaven, for the restoration of the earth, and for the shining of the lights that are upon the earth."
And Jacob called upon his mother Rebekah, and he said, "My heart has loved you, my son Jacob; may the God who is above the earth bless you."

May all the blessings that blessed Adam and Enoch, Noah and Shem be given to you. All that I have spoken and all that I have, I will give to you, that upon the earth as in heaven, may it endure upon you and your seed forever.
From this day forth, even unto eternity, may your God, the Lord, keep you from following Him, that the spirits of Satan may not afflict you and your seed.
May the Lord God be your Father, and you be His son. Be a leader for the people in all your generations, and may my son walk in peace.
Both departed in unity from Abraham; and Rebekah loved Jacob with all her heart and all her soul exceedingly more than Esau; and Isaac loved Esau more than Jacob.
In the second year of the fortieth, in the seventh month, in the first year, Abraham called upon Ishmael and his two sons, Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their children.
Keep the law of the Lord, and do righteousness, that each one may be as He is in all his ways, and that each one may love his neighbor, and that they may dwell in peace with one another.

To execute judgment and righteousness upon the earth, let them uphold their covenant, that they may be delivered from all death and iniquity; and let us cleanse ourselves from the iniquity and death among us, that the Lord may command them not to be scattered to the right or to the left.

If a woman, or a virgin, should entice you, cast her into the fire; for their eyes shall not see, nor their hearts shall not desire. The children of Canaan shall perish from the earth, and the daughters of Canaan shall not be taken as wives.

Concerning the judgment of the righteous and the judgment of Sodom, for their wickedness, for their death and iniquity, as it was decreed upon them, they shall be as one another in their destruction, as if death had come upon them.

And you, from all death and iniquity, keep yourselves from all transgression. Do not give your name to be called for destruction, nor let your lives be for destruction, nor let your children be put to death by the sword. You shall be as Sodom, and your children shall be as the children of Gomorrah.

Children, I have admonished you; love the God of heaven, and keep all His commandments; do not follow their idols and their iniquities. Do not make for yourselves the idols and images that are made for you; for they are vanity, and they have no breath in them; they are the work of human hands. All who trust in them are vanity, and do not be deceived by them; do not give them honor.

But you shall worship the Most High God, and always seek His face; always place your hope in Him; may He delight in you, and grant you His mercy, and bring forth the fruit of your labor and the harvest of your fields, and may He bless all your works, and justice and righteousness, and truth shall be done before Him.

May He bless your grain and your water; may He bless the seed of your cattle, the increase of your land, the offspring of your flocks and the offspring of your goats. You shall be a blessing upon the earth.
And all the peoples of the earth shall revere you. As I have spoken, may they be blessed in your name, and may your children be blessed.
And to his son Ishmael and to the sons of Keturah, he gave gifts, and sent them away from his son Isaac, while he yet lived. But to his son Isaac he gave all.

And Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah, and the sons of his son, went forth together. From the land of Paran, they dwelt in the wilderness, eastward, even unto the entrance of Babylon; and they were all one people. Their name was called Arab and they were called the children of Ishmael.
In this jubilee, in the seventh sabbath, in the sixth year, Abraham commanded his son Isaac, saying, "I am old; I have taken hold of my days, and I do not know the day of my death."

Behold, I am a hundred seventy-five years old; throughout all the days of my life, I have not forgotten the Lord God, and with my whole heart, I have done the will of my God, and in all my ways, I have walked in His paths. The living and holy God, who is more trustworthy than all, is the righteous God, and I keep my soul to do the will of my Creator, fleeing from idols.
For He is the God of righteousness; He judges all those who transgress His law and all those who break His covenant. In Him, there is no partiality, nor is there any acceptance of persons.

"My son, keep my commandments and my statutes, and preserve my judgments. Do not walk in the ways of the wicked, nor follow the abominations of the nations, nor eat the blood of any creature, whether of birds in the heavens or of beasts on the earth."

If you offer a peace offering, let it be accepted; sprinkle its blood upon the altar; and offer the fat of the offering along with the grain offering to the altar of the Lord, and let the offering that is sprinkled with oil be presented along with the drink offering, all in unity before the Lord, as a pleasing aroma, and let it be accepted as the fat of the offering burns upon the altar.
And all the fat that is upon the entrails, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the fat that is upon the liver, and the gallbladder, let it be offered up.

All these things shall be offered before the Lord as a pleasing aroma, and you shall present them as a burnt offering to the Lord, along with the grain offering and the drink offering. The flesh shall be eaten on that night and on the morrow.

And until the morrow, the sun shall not rise; for the Lord will not accept it, and it shall not be offered on the third day; for it is not chosen, and after that, it shall not be eaten. All those who eat it shall bear their iniquity.

In the books of the ancients, in the words of Enoch and Noah, I have found a writing that says, "In all your offerings, you shall add salt; and in the presence of the Lord, in every offering that is made, the covenant of salt shall not be removed."

"You shall only bring these woods to the altar for the offerings that are to be made thereon; take heed of these woods: senobar, keret, sagad, shenet, weira, wanzah, dokma, tedoh, zeyt, barsenat, tid, arboq, qega, shola."

Do not examine the nature of these trees; under the sacrifice that is offered in the sanctuary, do not take any wood that is broken or has been splintered. However, you may take the wood that is whole and beautiful, and also the wood from the new growth.

The altar is set apart; as it is ancient, there is no altar like it, so do not take any wood from it. However, the altar is unique; it will ascend to heaven, and apart from these trees, do not take any other.

Keep this command; my son, do all your work as I have commanded you. At all times, keep your body pure; before you go out to the sanctuary to offer sacrifices, wash in water; and before you approach the sacrifice, wash your hands and your feet.
When you present the sacrifice, at the time of your return, wash your hands and your feet. Let no blood be seen upon your body or your garments.

My son, guard yourself from blood; do not eat it; for blood is the life, and thus you shall not consume blood. Do not eat any blood; lest it be a judgment upon you, do not accept the blood of man; for the blood that is shed will destroy the land; and if you do not have blood upon you, do not be cleansed of the blood of man.

Do not accept the blood of man or the hand of violence. Before the Most High God, blood will return to blood. To keep you from all evil, and to deliver you from death, this protection shall be for good.
"My son, as the works of man are sin and wickedness, so their deeds are all corrupted and defiled, and I say that there is no righteousness among them."

Do not walk in their paths, nor follow their desires. Before the Most High God, do not commit a sin that leads to death. He will turn His face from you, and your iniquity will return upon you. From the earth, it will be removed; your seed will be destroyed from beneath the heavens; your name and your seed will perish from all the earth.

Keep away from all their works and all their abominations; keep the law of the Most High God; fulfill His will. Do all your work; in all your work, He will bless you. Throughout all the earth, and among all generations upon the earth, the righteous seed shall arise from you. Under heaven, in all times, my name and your name shall be remembered.

"My son, walk in peace; my God, and your God, the Most High Lord, will strengthen you to fulfill His will. May your children, and your children's children, be a blessing upon all the earth for eternal generations; may they be blessed in all righteousness." And he went out rejoicing.

In the forty-fourth year of the jubilee, in the first month, when Abraham had died, in the second year, it came to pass; that in the first month of the feast of the firstfruits, Isaac and Ishmael came from the well of Beer-lahai-roi unto their father Abraham.
And Abraham rejoiced, for his two sons had come. And the wealth of Isaac that was in Beer-lahai-roi was abundant; and Isaac would visit his father and return.
And in those days, Ishmael did not see his father, and they all came together in unity.

And Isaac offered the burnt offerings; and his father presented them upon the altar which he had made in Hebron. And he offered the offerings for the poor; and before his brother Ishmael, he rejoiced in gladness.

And Rebekah took fresh baked bread from the oven; and she brought it to her father-in-law Abraham, that he might bless the Creator of all, and she gave it to her son Jacob as the first fruits of the earth.

And Isaac blessed Abraham and said, "Let us eat and drink," and he gave the offerings for the poor into the hand of Jacob. And he blessed the earth and the heavens, and he praised the Almighty who created all things. Let them eat and drink, and let them give thanks to their Creator for their children.

And Abraham said, "This day has been made known to me; behold, I will bless you. And behold, I am a man of one hundred seventy-five years; I have grown old; my days are fulfilled; and all my years have been in peace; and the sword of the enemy has not prevailed against me."

And in all that You have given me, and in the life of my children, until this day, O my God, may You be set apart from all nations of the earth, from this day forth and for all generations until the end of the world, that I may be a chosen people and an inheritance for You; forgive me for Your servant and for my children.

And he called Jacob and said, "My son Jacob, may the God who created all bless you; may He strengthen you to do righteousness and to fulfill His will. And as He has willed, may you be a people of inheritance in your generation."
"And you, my son Jacob, draw near and sleep," and he drew near and slept.

And he said, "You, my son Jacob, are blessed. All your children are blessed before the Most High God for eternity. May He grant you the seed of the righteous; may they be sanctified among all the children of the earth. May nations serve you; and let all nations bow down before your seed; be a ruler before man, and shine among all the daughters."

At that time, your paths and the paths of your children shall be true to become a holy people. The Most High God, who blessed Noah and Adam, shall grant you all the blessings with which He blessed them. From generation to generation, until eternity, may they be upon you to sanctify your seed.

That you may find deliverance from all your sins, and be cleansed from all iniquity; may He strengthen you, that you may inherit all the land. To be a people for eternity, may He establish His covenant with you.
In all the days of the earth, may He be with you and your seed in truth and righteousness, O God.

"You, my son Jacob, heed my words; keep the command of your father, Abraham; separate yourself from the nations; do not partake with them, nor do as their works. For their works are cursed, and their ways are all cursed; their sacrifices are abominable, and do not be partakers with them."

They shall tremble for the beasts; they shall be given to the wicked; in the grave, they shall be consumed, and all their works are vanity and deceit. They have no heart to think; their eyes do not see. What is their work?
The wood: "You are my Creator; the stone: "You are my Lord; You are the one who saves me." How then do they worship? They have no heart.
"You, my son Jacob, may the Most High God help you; may the God of heaven bless you; may He keep you from all their iniquities and all their sins."

My son Jacob, take heed that you do not marry the daughters of Canaan. For their seed is for destruction upon the earth, and they are wicked in their deeds. Your son and your son's son shall all perish from the earth; and on the day of judgment, none shall be saved from them.

For those who worship idols and for all who are deceived, there is no hope in the living earth; they shall descend to Sheol, and they shall go to the place of judgment; upon the earth, they have no remembrance, and as the children of Sodom were cut off from the earth, so shall all who worship idols be cut off.
"O my son Jacob, fear not; O child of Abraham, be not dismayed; the Most High God shall keep thee from destruction; He shall deliver thee from all manner of sin."

"This house I have made for My name upon the earth, that it may be a dwelling for Me; it has been given to thee and to thy seed for everlasting generations. The house of Abraham shall be called by thy name."
"Thou shalt build My house, and My name shall be established before God forever; thy seed and thy name shall endure upon the earth for all generations." And thus he concluded and departed.
"And they both lay together in one bed, in unity. And Jacob lay beside his father, the father of Abraham. Seven times he slept; his heart was drawn to him, and indeed his heart was blessed by him."

"Thus he said, 'For everlasting generations, may it be blessed that our land shall give birth to a holy son; O Most High God, who is the God of all, and the Creator of all, deliver me from the wickedness of the wicked.'"

"With all my heart and in my supplication, bless my son Jacob. May thy mercy and abundant kindness be upon him and his seed throughout all generations. From this day forth, even unto everlasting, do not forsake him; let not thy grace depart from him."

"Keep them, that they may be blessed; sanctify a people that shall be thine inheritance; let thine eyes be upon him and his seed. From this day forth, even unto everlasting, bless them with all thy blessings."

"Thy covenant and thy mercy with him, and with his seed, let it be established upon the earth for all generations by thy perfect will." And he placed both of Jacob's hands upon his eyes; he gave thanks to the God of the heavens, and he covered his face.

His foot was lifted, and he fell into a deep sleep, as if he were dead; and he was gathered unto his fathers. In all this, Jacob lay beside him; he did not know that his father’s father, Abraham, had died.
And Jacob awoke from his sleep. Behold, Abraham was troubled; as if he were dead. And he said, "My father, my father." Yet there was no answer; for Abraham knew that he had died.

He arose from beside him and ran swiftly. He spoke to his mother, Rebekah. And Rebekah went by night to Isaac; they went in unity. And Jacob was with them. He held lamps in his hand. And as they went, they found Abraham’s head, having been wounded. And Isaac fell before his father and wept, not knowing.

And a great cry was heard in the house of Abraham. His son Ishmael arose and went to his father Abraham, and he wept before his father Abraham. He and all the household of Abraham wept a great weeping. His sons, Isaac and Ishmael, were in the house of his wife, Sarah, and they mourned beside her. And all the household mourned for forty days.
Isaac and Ishmael, and all their children, mourned greatly in their places. The mourning of Abraham was heavy.

He lived three Jubilees and four weeks; this is one hundred seventy-five years, and the time he lived was completed. He was gathered; his time was fulfilled. The days of the former men who lived were nine Jubilees.
After the flood, however, to preserve the Jubilees and hasten to the end, except for Abraham, many were raised from their labors, and they began to be delivered from the days of the nine Jubilees.
But Abraham was perfect in his works with the Lord, and all his days were filled with truth and joy.

Behold, from the multitude of troubles he arose, until he was gathered, the four Jubilees did not end in life. And he kept his age; from today until the day of judgment, all the children who will arise will be two Jubilees without being diminished, they will hasten and be gathered.
From their offspring arose their knowledge; their perfect knowledge will be separated.
In those days, if a man were to have a jubilee and a jubilee companion, it would be said of him, "He has lived a long time."

However, the majority of the time of this age is filled with sickness, weakness, and suffering; peace is not found; in affliction there is affliction, in pain there is pain, in suffering there is suffering, in evil testimony there is evil testimony, in disease there is disease.

Likewise, all evil judgment shall prevail; and this is with the following afflictions: fever, weakness, death, sleep, decay, disease of the belly, pestilence, death, sorrow, suffering, all affliction; and all these shall come upon this wicked generation, for they are the result of their evil deeds.
At that time, they shall say, "The times of our forefathers were abundant; they lasted until a thousand years; and they were good."

Behold, our time of life, however, if a man were to say he has lived a long time, it is seven years; and if it were to increase greatly, it is eighty years. All is evil; and in this wicked generation, there is no peace.

In this generation, the children shall oppress their fathers and their mothers. Because of sin and iniquity, because of their transgressions, they shall be great iniquities, keeping the commandments and the statutes, and all the law, that they may do; and between them and Him, God shall remember the covenant He made with them.

All evil deeds shall not cease until they are done, nor shall they turn to the right or to the left. Every transgression shall speak of wickedness. Their works are all abominable, and they are a cause of distress. Their paths are crooked; they are destructive; they are ruinous.

"Behold, the earth shall perish because of their works. They have no seed of the vine; they have no oil; all their works are in vain, for beasts and birds and all the fish of the sea shall perish together with the children of men."

These shall be with these, the youth with the mothers, and the mothers with the youth, the poor with the rich, the small with the great, the oppressor with the judge, they shall contend concerning the law and the covenant.

The commandments and the covenant, the feast and the monthly observance, the sabbath and the jubilee, all judgments have been neglected; from their paths, they shall return to the sword of violence. But those who keep the law shall not return until much blood has been shed upon the earth. These shall rise against these. The righteous shall not return from their iniquities.

Each one shall take all the money of his neighbor to be prepared for the feast; they shall be called by a great name. However, in truth, it is not so, nor is it in righteousness; by their wickedness and their destruction, they shall defile My holy ones.

"In that generation, the work shall be a strong condemnation from the Lord. For the sword and for punishment, for destruction and for dwelling, for calamity shall be given to them; upon them shall be poured out the mercy and forgiveness that belong not to the nations."

They shall be cut off from all the children of men, for they are wicked and mighty; whether it be a woman or a child, they shall not be spared; they shall bring strife upon Israel, and upon Jacob they shall commit iniquity; much blood shall be shed upon the earth; there shall be none to gather it, and none to bury it.

"In those days, they shall cry out; they shall be delivered from the hand of the sinners of the nations. However, there shall be none to save them. The heads of the children shall be struck with a curse. The three hundred children shall be as a great multitude, and they shall be seen as a great multitude. Their stature shall be diminished in anguish and in distress."

In those days, the children shall begin to seek the law, and to search for the commandment, and to return to the path of truth. The days shall multiply and be increased; the children of men shall multiply from generation to generation; their days shall be prolonged until they come to a thousand years, and from many days until many years, day by day they shall multiply.
There shall be no sorrow; there shall be no age that shall grow old; all shall be children and youths. All shall fulfill their days, and they shall dwell in peace and joy.
There shall be no sorrow; all their days shall be days of blessing and of prosperity, and no evil shall be found to destroy.

"At that time, the Lord shall deliver His servants; they shall arise, and in the world, they shall see much peace; their enemies shall be cast away, and they shall be set free. The righteous shall not be forsaken, and they shall give thanks. Until the end of the world, they shall rejoice exceedingly. They shall see all the judgment that has been done to their enemies and all their deliverance. Their bones shall rest upon the earth; their souls shall abound in joy."
The Lord, who executes judgment, shall be known, and for all who love Him, He shall grant forgiveness in hundreds and in thousands for the age that shall be counted.
Moses, you also write this thing; for thus it is written; it shall be a law for the generation of the world, and in heaven, they shall write prayers.

And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that the Lord blessed his son Isaac; and he arose from Beer-lahai-roi, and dwelt in the land of the south, and there he lived for seven years in the first year of the third jubilee.
In the fourth jubilee, in the first year, during the time of Abraham, there was a great famine in all the land, and Jacob was in Egypt, and Esau went to the land of Edom.
And his brother Jacob said unto him, "Give me of this red pottage, for I am faint."
And he said, "Sell me your birthright, and I will give you this pottage and some of this red meat."
And Esau said within himself, "I am at the point of death; what profit shall this birthright do to me?" And he said unto Jacob, "Behold, I have given you my birthright."

And Jacob said, "Swear to me this day." And he swore unto him; and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentils; and he did eat and drink, and rose up and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
Therefore was Esau called Edom, because Jacob gave him bread and pottage of lentils.
And Jacob increased, but Esau diminished before him.
And there was a famine in the land, and in the second year of this jubilee, Isaac went down to Egypt to sojourn there; and he went unto Abimelech, king of the Philistines.

And God appeared unto him and said, "Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell you of. Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for unto you and unto your seed will I give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I swore unto your father Abraham; and I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and I will give unto your seed all these countries."
Your father, having heard my words and my command, my law and my ordinance, and having kept my covenant, may all the nations of the earth be blessed through your seed.

Now hear my words and my command; dwell in this land.” Three years he resided in Gerar. And Abimelech, concerning him and all his wealth, commanded, saying, “Whoever takes him or his wealth shall surely die.”

And Isaac sowed in the land of Philistia, and he reaped in that year; and he had sheep and oxen, and servants and camels in abundance. There was much prosperity. And in the land of Philistia, he sowed seed.

A hundredfold he reaped. And Isaac was exceedingly prosperous. The men of Philistia envied him. While Abraham was alive, the wells which his servants had dug were stopped up; but after Abraham died, the men of Philistia filled them with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Depart from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
And Isaac, in the seventh year of the famine, arose and went to Gerar.

The wells which his father Abraham had dug, the Philistines had stopped up after the death of his father Abraham; and they filled them with earth. And he called them by the names which his father Abraham had called them. And Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of living water.

And the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” And Isaac said, “They have quarreled with us;” therefore he named that well “Esek.” And they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also; and he named it “Sitnah.”
And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; and he named it “Rehoboth.”
And Isaac said, “Today the Lord has made room for us; we shall be fruitful in the land.” And he went up from there to Beer-sheba in the first year of the forty-first jubilee.

And it came to pass that in that night, in the first month, the Lord revealed Himself, saying, “I am the God of thy father Abraham; I will dwell with thee, and be not afraid; I will honor thee; and for thy friend, for the seed of Abraham, I will multiply thee as the sand of the sea.”

And he called upon the name of the Lord, having built an altar at that place where his father Abraham had previously built an altar. He offered sacrifices unto the Lord, and he dug a well, and he found good water.
And the servants of Isaac dug another well, but they found no water. And they went and told Isaac that they had not found water.

And Isaac said, “This day I shall be a cause of contention with the Philistines; for this matter has become a matter for us.” And he called the name of that place “Esek,” because they had striven with him.

And Isaac sought peace with them on that day, as they were in conflict; and Isaac dealt with the men of the Philistines. And he said, “In the day of strife and anger, the man of the Philistines is fierce; may the Lord deliver them from all nations, and from their wrath and anger, and from their strife and fury.”
For the children in their time shall be as the enemies of the earth, and they shall be as the sword of the enemy; and the righteous shall be judged from heaven beneath.
The seed of the Philistines shall be uprooted from the earth for destruction and for extermination, and there shall be none left for them. In the day of judgment, there shall be no escape.

For all that remains upon the earth shall have no name or seed; until they ascend to heaven, from there they shall descend; and if they remain upon the earth, then they shall be uprooted; and among the nations, if they wander, then they shall be destroyed.
And if they descend to Sheol, there their punishment shall be great; for there shall be no peace.
Those who seek to destroy their bodies shall be cast into the streets, and there shall be no name or seed remaining upon the earth. They shall go to eternal destruction.
"The earth shall be consumed, for on the day of judgment, it is for Him to render account; thus it is written in heaven concerning Him: 'He has been forsaken.'"

In this, Rebekah spoke to her son Jacob, saying, “My son, do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, as your brother Esau did. Their deeds are all evil and their ways are wicked, and they have caused me great distress; for their works are corrupt, and in them there is no truth.”
“My son, I truly love you. My heart and my goodness shall guard you by day and by night.”

“Now, my son, heed my voice and do according to my command. Do not take a wife from the daughters of this land, from the house of your father, nor from your kin, but take a wife from my family. May the Almighty God bless you; and your children shall be true children, and your seed shall be holy.”

After this, Jacob spoke to his mother Rebekah, saying, “Mother, behold, I am a man of seven years; I know not any woman; I have not married; I have not taken a wife. As for the daughters of Canaan, I have not thought of taking a wife from among them, for I have considered the command of our father Abraham, and I do not think of taking a wife from the daughters of Canaan, but I shall take a wife from my father's kin.”
“For your brother, for the daughters of Laban, I have heard beforehand. And from them I have taken my heart and set it upon them.”

“Therefore, let it not be a burden to me; in all my ways, in the days of my life, let me not perish; let me be guarded in my body. For concerning the wickedness and the evil deeds of my father Abraham, I have wept and lamented; and I have lamented with all these things. My brother, concerning the two wives, one of them I have taken as a sister, and while he was speaking to me and reasoning with me, it has been twenty years.”

“And I too, as my brother has done, I shall not do; for in my days, I have not taken a wife from the daughters of Canaan, nor shall I do evil as my brother has done. Mother, do not fear; as I do according to your command, and as I walk in righteousness, I will not perish in my ways forever.”
After this, she lifted her voice to heaven; she spread her hands; and she praised the Almighty God who created the heavens and the earth; and she offered perfect praise unto Him.”

“Thus she said, ‘Blessed be my God, who has given me a holy seed, Jacob; may the Lord be praised forever; may His name be blessed forever. Yours is he, and to you shall he be, for all generations, even unto many ages.’”
“O Lord, bless them. And let them receive the blessing of righteousness in my presence.”
ያንጊዜም መንፈስ ቅዱስ ወርዶ በአንደበቷ አናገራት፤ ሁለቱን እጆችዋንም በያዕቆብ ራስ ላይ አኖረች። እንዲህም አለች፥ “የጽድቅ ጌታ፥ የዓለማት አምላክ አንተ የተመሰገንህ ነህ።

ልጄ ሆይ ከሰው ልጅ ሁሉ ለይቶ አንተን ይባርክ። የጽድቅን መንገድ ይስጥህ፤ ለዘርህም ጽድቅን ይግለጥለት፤ በሕይወትህ ሳለህም ልጆችህን ያብዛልህ፤ በዓመቱም ወሮች ቍጥር ዐሥራ ሁለት ይሁኑ። ልጆቻቸውም ይብዙ፤ ከሰማይ ከዋክብት ይልቅ ይብዙ፤ ቍጥራቸውም ከባሕር አሸዋ ይብዛ። ለአብርሃም ይሰጣት ዘንድ፥ ከእርሱም በኋላ በዘመኑ ሁሉ ለዘሩ ይሰጣቸው ዘንድ እንደ ተናገረ ያችን የተወደደች ምድር ይስጣቸው።

ለዘለዓለም እጅ አድርገው ይዘዋት ይኑሩ። ልጄ ሆይ፥ በሕይወት ሳለሁ የተባረከ ልጅን ልይ፤ ዘርህ ሁሉ የተባረከና፥ የተቀደሰ ዘር ይሁን፤ በሕይወቷ ሳለች የእናትህን ልቡና እንዳሳረፍህ የእናትህ ማኅፀን እንዲህ ትመርቅህ፤ ማኅፀኔና ጡቴ አንተን ይመርቁ፤ አፌና አንደበቴም ፈጽመው አንተን ያመስግኑ፤ ፈጽመህ ብዛ፤ በዓለሙም ሁሉ ምላ። ዘርህም በሰማይና በምድር ስፋት በዓለሙ ሁሉ ፍጹም ይሁን፤ ዘርህንም ደስ ይበለው።
በታላቅ ሰላም ቀንም ሰላም ይሁንለት። ስምህና ዘርህ እስከ ብዙ ዘመን ድረስ ይኑር፤ ልዑል አምላክም አምላካቸው ይሁን፤ የጽድቅ አምላክም ከእነርሱ ጋር ይኑር። መቅደሱም በዓለሙ ሁሉ በእነርሱ ይሠራ። የሚመርቅህ የተመረቀ ይሁን፤ በሐሰት የምትረግምህ ሰውነት ሁሉ የተረገመች ትሁን፤”
እርሷም ሳመችው፤ እንዲህም አለችው፥ “የእናትህ ልቡና እንደሚወድህ፥ ማኅፀንዋም በአንተ ደስ እንደሚለው፥ እንደሚመርቅህም የዓለሙ ሁሉ ጌታ አንተን ይውደድህ።” ከዚያ በኋላ ከመመረቅ ዝም አለች።
በዚህ ሱባዔ በሰባተኛው ዓመት ይስሐቅ ታላቁን ልጁን ዔሳውን ጠርቶ እንዲህ አለው፥ “ልጄ ሆይ፥ እኔ አረጀሁ፤ እነሆ፥ ዐይኖች ለማየት ፈዝዘዋል፤ የምሞትባትን ቀን አላውቅም።
አሁንም የምታድንበትን ጦርህንና ጎራንጎሬህን፥ ቀስትህንም ይዘህ ወደ ምድረ በዳ ውጣ። አደንም አድነህና አጥምደህ አምጣልኝ፤ ልጄ! ሰውነቴ የምትወድደውን መብል አዘጋጅተህ እበላ ዘንድ አምጣልኝ፤ ሳልሞትም ሰውነቴ ትመርቅህ” አለው። ርብቃም ይስሐቅ ለዔሳው ሲነግረው ነገሩን ትሰማ ነበር።
ዔሳውም አጥምዶ ይይዝና ለአባቱ ያመጣ ዘንድ ወደ ምድረ በዳ ገሥግሦ ሄደ።
ርብቃም ልጅዋን ያዕቆብን ጠርታ እንዲህ አለችው፥ “አባትህ ይስሐቅ፦ አደን አድነህ አምጥተህ የምበላውን አዘጋጅልኝ፤ በልች ሳልሞት በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ልመርቅህ ብሎ ከወንድምህ ከዔሳው ጋር ሲነጋገር ሰማሁት።
አሁንም፥ ልጄ ሆይ፥ እኔ የማዝዝህን ነገር ስማ፤ ወደ መንጋህ ሄደህ የአማሩ ሁለት የፍየል ጠቦቶችን አምጣልኝ፤ እንደሚወድደውም አድርጌ ለአባትህ ምግብ ላዘጋጃቸው፤ ሳይሞትም በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ይመርቅህ ዘንድ፥ ለአባትህ አቅርበህለት ይብላ፤ የተመረቅህም ትሆናለህ።”

And Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, "I do not wish to be cursed for the sake of my father’s meal and the joy it brings him. Yet, my mother! I fear that he may not recognize my voice. He will surely treat me as a deceiver, and I shall bring upon myself a curse instead of a blessing."

And his mother Rebekah said, "My son, let the curse fall upon me, only obey my voice." And Jacob heeded the words of his mother Rebekah; he went and fetched two young goats from the flock, and brought them to his mother. And she prepared them in the manner that his father Isaac loved.

And Rebekah took the best garments of her elder son Esau, which were in her house, and put them upon her younger son Jacob. And she placed the skins of the goats upon his hands and upon the smooth part of his neck. And she gave the savory food and the bread which she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob.

And Jacob went to his father Isaac and said, "My father!" And he answered, "Here am I. Who art thou, my son?" And Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou hast commanded me. Arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me."
And Isaac said to his son, "How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son?" And Jacob said, "Because the Lord thy God brought it to me."
And Isaac said, "Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not."
And Jacob went near to Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, "The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau."
And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands; so he blessed him.
And he said, "Art thou my very son Esau?" And he said, "I am."
And he said, "Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee." And he brought it near to him, and he did eat; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
መብሉንም አቀረበለትና በላ። ወይንንም አቀረበለትና ጠጣ።
አባቱ ይስሐቅም፥ “ልጄ ሆይ! ቀርበህ ሳመኝ” አለው።
ቀርቦም ሳመው። ደስ የሚያሰኝ የልብሱን መዓዛ አሸተተ። መረቀውም። እንዲህም አለ፥ “እነሆ፥ የልጄ የልብሱ መዓዛ እግዚአብሔር እንደ ባረከው እንደ መስክ መዓዛ ነው። እግዚአብሔር ይስጥህ፤ ከሰማይ ጠልና ከምድር ጠል ያብዛህ፤ ስንዴውንና ዘይቱን ያብዛልህ።
አሕዛብ ይገዙልህ፤ ሕዝቡም ይስገዱልህ፤ ለወንድምህም ጌታ ሁነው፤ የእናትህም ልጆች ይስገዱልህ። እግዚአብሔር እኔን የባረከባቸው፥ አባቴ አብርሃምንም የባረከባቸው በረከቶች ሁሉ ለአንተ ይሁኑህ፤ እስከ ዘለዓለምም ድረስ ለልጆችህ ይሁኑ። የሚረግምህ የተረገመ ነው፥ የሚመርቅህም የተመረቀ ነው” አለው።
ይስሐቅ ልጁን ያዕቆብን መርቆት ከጨረሰ በኋላ እንዲህ ሆነ።
ከወጣም በኋላ እንዲህ ሆነ፤ ያዕቆብም ከአባቱ ከይስሐቅ ዘንድ ወጥቶ ተሸሸገ። ወንድሙ ዔሳው ግን ከአደኑ ደረሰ፤ እርሱም መብልን አዘጋጅቶ ለአባቱ አቀረበ፤ አባቱንም፥ “አባቴ ሆይ፥ ሰውነትህ ትመርቀኝ ዘንድ አደን አድኜ ከአመጣሁልህ ተነሥ ብላ” አለው።
አባቱ ይስሐቅም፥ “አንተ ማን ነህ?” አለው። “እኔ የበኵር ልጅህ ዔሳው ነኝ፤ እንዳዘዝኸኝ አደረግሁ” አለው።
ይስሐቅም እጅግ ፈጽሞ ተደነቀ፥ “አደን አድኖ አምጥቶልኝ አንተ ሳትመጣ ከሁሉ በልች የመረቅሁት ይህ ማን ነው? የተመረቀ ይሁን፤ ዘሩም እስከ ዘለዓለም ድረስ የተመረቀ ይሁን” አለው።
ዔሳውም የአባቱን የይስሐቅን ነገር በሰማ ጊዜ እንዲህ ሆነ። በታላቅ ቃል እጅግ ምርር ብሎ ጮኸ፤ አባቱን፥ “አባቴ ሆይ፥ እኔንም መርቀኝ” አለው።
“ወንድምህ በተንኰል መጥቶ በረከትህን ወሰደብህ፤” አለው።

"Jacob said, 'Since you have called me by my name, I have come to know you today. Behold, this is the second time. Previously, he took my birthright; now he has taken my blessing. Father, have you not reserved a blessing for me?'"

Isaac replied to Esau, saying, "Behold, I have made him lord over you; and all his brethren I have given to him as servants. And with grain and wine I have sustained him. What then shall I do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father Isaac, "Father, is there but one blessing for you? Father, bless me also." And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
Isaac answered and said to him, "Behold, your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; and by your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother."
"But if you shall become restless, and you shall break his yoke from off your neck, you shall surely die. And your seed shall be destroyed from under heaven."

Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, "The days of mourning for my father are approaching; then I will kill my brother Jacob." The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah.

Rebekah called Jacob her younger son and said to him, "Behold, your brother Esau seeks to kill you. Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; arise, flee to your brother Laban in Haran; and stay with him a few days until your brother's fury turns away, until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you from there. Why should I be deprived of you both in one day?"
Jacob said, "I will not be afraid; if he seeks to kill me, I will be killed."
"You shall not bear all your children in one day, lest it be that I have not given birth at all," she said.
Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, "Father is as a man who is blind; behold, you know that my skin is smooth; and his eyes are dim, so he will not see."
ከእናንተ ተለይቼ ትቼው ብሄድ በፊቱ ክፉ ይሆናል፤ አባቴም ተቈጥቶ ይረግመኛልና አልሄድም፤ ቢያሰናብተኝ ግን ያንጊዜ እሄዳለሁ፤” አላት።
ርብቃም ያዕቆብን፥ “እኔ ገብች እነግረዋለሁ፤ ያሰናብትሃልም” አለችው።
ርብቃም ወደ ይስሐቅ ገብታ ይስሐቅን እንዲህ አለችው፥ “ዔሳው ለእርሱ ሚስት አድርጎ ከአገባቸው ከሁለቱ ከኬጢ ልጆች የተነሣ ኑሮዬን ጠላሁ፤ ያዕቆብ እንደነዚህ ከአሉ ከሀገሪቱ ሴቶች ልጆች ለእርሱ ሚስት ከአገባ የከነዓን ሴቶች ልጆች ክፉዎች ናቸውና እንደ ምን እኖራለሁ?”
ይስሐቅም ልጁን ያዕቆብን ጠርቶ መረቀው፤ መከረውም፥ “ከከነዓን ሴቶች ልጆች ሁሉ ሚስት አታግባ፥ ተነሥተህ ወደ መስጴጦምያ ወደ እናትህ አባት ወደ ባቱኤል ቤት ሂድ፤

ከዚያም ከእናትህ ወንድም ከላባ ሴቶች ልጆች ሚስት አግባ። የሰማይ አምላክ ይባርክህ። ፈጽሞም ያብዛህ። የአሕዛብ ጌታ ሁን። ተሰድደህ ትኖርባት የነበረች ሀገርን፥ እግዚአብሔርም ለአብርሃም የሰጣትን ምድር ሁላ ትወርሳት ዘንድ የአባቴን የአብርሃምን በረከት ለአንተና ከአንተም በኋላ ለዘርህ ይስጥህ። ልጄ ሆይ፥ በሰላም ሂድ” አለው፥
ይስሐቅም ያዕቆብን አሰናበተው። ወደ ያዕቆብ እናት ወደ ርብቃ ወንድም ወደ ሶርያዊው ሰው ወደ ባቱኤል ልጅ ወደ ላባ ዘንድ ወደ መስጴጦምያ ሄደ።
ያዕቆብ ወደ መስጴጦምያ ለመሄድ ከተነሣ በኋላ እንዲህ ሆነ። ልጅዋ ከሄደ በኋላ የርብቃ ልብዋ አዝኖ ታለቅስ ነበር።
ይስሐቅም ርብቃን፥ “እኅቴ ሆይ ስለ ልጂሽ ስለ ያዕቆብ አታልቅሺ። በሰላም ሄዶ በሰላም ይመለሳልና፤ ልዑል አምላክም ከክፉ ሁሉ ይጠብቀዋልና፤ ከእርሱም ጋር ይኖራል፤ በዘመኑም ሁሉ አይለየውም፤ ወደ እኛ በሰላም እስኪመለስ ድረስ በሄደበት ሁሉ ጎዳናው እንዲቀናለት አውቃለሁና።
በሰላም እናየዋለን፤ እኅቴ ሆይ፥ ስለ እርሱ አትፍሪ። እርሱ በመንገዱ የቀና ነውና፥ ፍጹምም ነውና፤ የታመነ ሰውም ነውና፤ አይወድቅምና አታልቅሺ” አላት። ይስሐቅም ስለ ልጅዋ ስለ ያዕቆብ ርብቃን ያረጋጋት ነበር። እርሱንም መረቀው።

And Jacob departed from Beersheba, and went toward Haran; and he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set. And he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the Lord stood above it, and said, "I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed."

And it came to pass, when he was at that place, and he tarried there all night, that he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the Lord stood above it, and said, "I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed."

And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the Lord stood above it, and said, "I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed."

And the Lord spoke to Jacob, saying, "I am the God of thy father Abraham, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed. And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed."

And behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of."
And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, "Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not."
And he was afraid, and said, "How dreadful is this place! This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.

And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, "If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God."
And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee."
"This shall be a sign for me, that I have set up this stone as a pillar; it shall be the house of God. And of all that You give me, I will surely give a tenth to You."
And he arose and went to Mesopotamia, to the east, to his brother, and to Laban.

And he dwelt with him; and concerning his daughter, concerning Rachel, he purchased a single maidservant; and in the third year, in the first year, he said, "Give me my wife, for I have served you for seven years for her."

And Laban said to Jacob, "I will give you my daughter." And Laban made a feast; and he gave his elder daughter to Jacob to be his wife, that she might serve him; and he also gave him her maidservant to serve her.
But Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and he went in to her; but behold, Leah was tender-eyed.

And Jacob was angry with Laban, and said, "What you have given me for Leah is not right; is it not for Rachel? Why have you dealt thus with me? Why have you deceived me? Take your daughter and go; for I have been wronged."
Leah's eyes were weak, but Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah; nevertheless, her appearance was very beautiful. Rachel was indeed beautiful in form and appearance.
And Laban said to Jacob, "It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn. It is not right to do this; it is not proper. The firstborn shall be given before the younger."
Thus, concerning one who does this, a curse shall be written against him in heaven.
For this deed is wicked in the sight of God; therefore, the one who commits this deed shall not be justified.
And you, for the children of Israel: It is indeed very evil, and I command that you do not commit this matter; do not give the small ones without giving the great ones first.

And he said to Jacob, "The feast of her marriage shall be completed in seven days. Moreover, I will give you Rachel for another seven years, if you will keep watch over my flocks as you did in the beginning; then I will give her to you."

The feast of Leah's marriage was completed in seven days, and after that time, she gave Rachel to Jacob for another seven years. And for Rachel, she gave her maidservant, that she might serve her. Leah was given in exchange for Rachel, and thus, for Rachel, another seven years were completed.
And the Lord opened Leah's womb, and she conceived; and she bore a son to Jacob, and in the third month of the first year, on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month, he named him Reuben.
And the Lord saw that Leah was unloved, but Rachel was loved; therefore, Leah's womb was opened.
And Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived; and she bore him a second son; and in the tenth month of the twentieth day of the eleventh month, he named him Simeon.
In this month, in the third year, Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived; and she bore him a third son; and in the first month, she named him Levi.
In this month, in the sixth year, Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived; and she bore him a fourth son; and in the fourth month, on the fifteenth day of the first year, he named him Judah.
She had not given birth, and in all this, Rachel was envious of Leah. And she said to Jacob, "Give me children, or else I die."
And Jacob said, "Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of your womb?"
ራሔልም ልያ ለያዕቆብ አራት ልጆች ሮቤልንና ስምዖንን፥ ሌዊንና ይሁዳን እንደ ወለደች ባየች ጊዜ፥ “ወደ ባሪያዬ ወደ ባላን ግባ፤ ትፀንሳለች፤ ወንድ ልጅንም ትወልድልኛለች” አለችው።
ያዕቆብም ወደ ባላን ገባ፤ እርስዋም ፀነሰች፤ ወንድ ልጅንም ወለደችለት፤ በሦስተኛው ሱባዔ በስድስተኛው ዓመት በስድስተኛው ወር በዘጠነኛው ቀን ስሙን ዳን አለው።
ያዕቆብም ዳግመኛ ወደ ባላን ገባ፤ እርስዋም ፀነሰች፤ ለያዕቆብም ዳግመኛ ወንድ ልጅን ወለደችለት። በአራተኛው ሱባዔ በሁለተኛው ዓመት በሰባተኛው ወር በአምስተኛው ቀን ራሔል ስሙን ንፍታሌም አለችው።
ልያም እንደ መከነች፥ ልጅም እንደማትወልድ በአየች ጊዜ እርስዋ በራሔል ቀናች፤ እርስዋም አገልጋይዋን ዘለፋን ለያዕቆብ ሚስት ትሆነው ዘንድ ሰጠችው። እርስዋም ጸነሰች፤ ወንድ ልጅንም ወለደችለት። በአራተኛው ሱባዔ በሦስተኛው ዓመት በስምንተኛው ወር በዐሥራ ሁለተኛው ቀን ስሙን ጋድ አለችው።
ዳግመኛም ወደ እርስዋ ገባ፤ እርስዋም ፀነሰች፤ ሁለተኛ ወንድ ልጅንም ወለደችለት፤ በአራተኛው ሱባዔ በአምስተኛው ዓመት በዐሥራ አንደኛው ወር በሁለተኛው ቀን ልያ ስሙን አሴር አለችው።
ያዕቆብም ወደ ልያ ገባ፤ እርስዋም ፀነሰች፤ ለያዕቆብም ወንድ ልጅን ወለደችለት፤ በአራተኛው ሱባዔ በአራተኛው ዓመት በአምስተኛው ወር በአራተኛው ቀን ስሙን ይሳኮር አለችው፤ ለሞግዚትም ሰጠችው።
ያዕቆብም ዳግመኛ ወደ እርስዋ ገባ፤ ፀነሰች፤ ወንድና ሴት ሁለት ልጆችን ወለደችለት። በአርባ አራተኛው ኢዮቤልዩ በስድስተኛው ሱባዔ በሰባተኛው ዓመት በሰባተኛው ወር የወንዱን ስም ዛብሎን አለችው፤ የሴቲቱን ስም ዲና አለቻት።
እግዚአብሔርም ራሔልን ይቅር አላት፤ ማኅፀንዋም ተከፈተ፤ ፀነሰችም ወንድ ልጅንም ወለደች፤ በአራተኛው ሱባዔ በስድስተኛው ዓመት በአራተኛው ወር መባቻ ስሙን ዮሴፍ አለችው።
ዮሴፍም በተወለደ ጊዜ ያዕቆብ ላባን፥ “ሚስቶችንና ልጆችን ስጠኝ፤ ወደ አባቴ ወደ ይስሐቅ ልሂድ፤ ስለ ሁለቱ ልጆችህ ለአንተ የተገዛሁላቸውን ዘመኖች ፈጽሜአለሁና ቤት እሠራለሁ፤ ወደ አባቴም ቤት እሄዳለሁ” አለው።
ላባም ያዕቆብን፥ “በደመወዝህ ከእኔ ጋር ተቀመጥ፤ ዳግመኛም መንጋዎችን ጠብቅልኝ፤ ደመወዝህንም ውሰድ፤” አለው።
And the ram, born white, was to become a lamb, and the goat and the ram, in all the goats, the lamb shall be given, and they shall contend with one another.

And in all the goats, the one that has a mark, the ram shall be born; and the male goats shall begin to be born in those that have a mark. The one that has a mark is for Jacob, and the one that has no mark is for Laban.
And Jacob's wealth increased greatly; he acquired cattle and goats, both male and female, and he begot a son and a daughter.
And Laban and his sons were with Jacob on that day. And Laban gathered his goats from him; and he began to regard them with an evil eye.
And Rachel, after she had borne Joseph, thus it was; Laban went to shear his sheep. And for three days they were distant from him.

And Jacob, as Laban went to shear his sheep, lifted up his eyes and called to Leah and Rachel, to come to him, for it was fitting for them to speak to him. All that he had seen in a dream, he recounted to them, and he said that they should return to their father's house.
And they said, "Wherever you go, we will go with you."
And Jacob gave thanks to the God of his father Isaac, and to the God of his grandfather Abraham.
And he arose and set his wives and children upon camels; and he gathered all his wealth. And he departed, and he came to the land of Gilead.
And Jacob concealed his thoughts from Laban, and he did not tell him. In the fourth year, in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, Jacob returned to Gilead. And Laban followed after him.

In the third month, on the twenty-third day, Jacob encountered Laban in the land of Gilead. In a dream by night, God spoke to him, saying, "Do not do anything evil against Jacob," and He did not permit Laban to harm Jacob; thus, Laban spoke to Jacob.
And in that month, on the twenty-fifth day, Jacob was afraid of Laban, and all the people who were with him were filled with fear.

One did not desire to harm the other, for on that day, in Gilead, Jacob spoke to Laban; and Laban spoke to Jacob. And there was a witness, for he made a heap; therefore, that place was called "Jegar Sahadutha."

Formerly, the land of Gilead was called the land of the Rephaim; for it was the land of the Rephaim. Their stature was ten cubits, and those of nine cubits, seven cubits, and eight cubits were born of the Rephaim. Their dwelling was from the land of the children of Ammon, even unto the mountain of Hermon.
And their cities were Heshbon and Ataroth, Adriah and Mesha, and they were very wicked; and because of their evil deeds, the Lord destroyed them.

Concerning them, a great wickedness was committed, for the Amorites dwelt in their land. Today, there is no one who has accomplished all their sins. After this, there was no longer a multitude of days upon the earth.

And Jacob returned to Laban; and he went to the land of the east. And Jacob returned to the land of Gilead. In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, he fled from Laban. And on that day, his brother Esau came to him, and they embraced.
And he departed from him and went to the land of Seir. But Jacob dwelt in tents.

In this Jubilee, in the fifth year, in the first year, he crossed the Jordan and settled in the valley of Jordan. From the edge of the wilderness, beginning from the sea of salt, even unto Dothan and unto the house of Sion, even unto the region of Amon, he was a shepherd.

For his mother, Rebekah, during the two times of the tenth month, between the seed and the harvest, between the sowing and the reaping, between the winter and the summer, four times a year, she would send to Abraham's tent.
And Isaac returned from the region of the Negev and dwelt in the land of his father Abraham, for he had separated himself from his son Esau and there he resided.
And Jacob, as he journeyed toward Mesopotamia, took a wife from among the daughters of Esau. This woman was the daughter of Ishmael. He gathered all the tents of his father and also his wives.
And he dwelt in the mountains of Seir. His father Isaac had only departed from the region of the Negev.
And Isaac also departed from the region of the Negev and dwelt in Hebron, in the cave of his father Abraham.
And from that time, Jacob would send to his mother and father all that he had, and at every time he would send that which they desired.

And Jacob, with a perfect heart and a perfect soul, would be remembered. In the sixth year of the sabbatical cycle, in the first year, he went to the east of the land of Sekim, and in the fourth month, he departed in peace.

And there came the son of Jacob, Dinah, to the land of the ruler, to Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite; and he took her and lay with her. And she was a young woman, being about twelve years of age. And she was given to him as a wife from her father and her brothers.

And Jacob was angry. For he had defiled his sister Dinah, and his sons were in the field with the cattle, and they heard it; and they were grieved, and they were very angry, and they would not speak to him.
Simeon and Levi took their swords and went into the city, and they struck all the males in the city.
And they killed every male in the city. Not one man did they spare. And they took their sister Dinah, for she had been defiled.

From this day forth, henceforth, let it not be done to the sons of Israel to defile themselves in this manner. For because of the defilement done to Israel, all the men of Shechem were slain by the sword, and in heaven their cry has been heard, and their punishment has been decreed.

By the sword they were slain; and upon them shall come the punishment; that the defilement of Israel shall not be done henceforth among the sons of Israel. May God bring upon the sons of Jacob His judgment.

If it be a son of Israel, or if it be a sister, let it be given to every man born of the nations; and if there be a man who desires it, let him die. For he has committed sin, and he has brought defilement upon Israel; let them be slain with the sword.

And the woman shall be called by her father's name, and she shall be burned with fire; and she shall be cast out from Israel. For Israel is holy unto the Lord, and throughout all generations upon the earth, there shall not be found a woman who is a sinner among Israel.

Let every man who has wrought wickedness die; let them be cast out with stones. For concerning the sons of Israel, it has been decreed in heaven: thus has it been written; and every man who defiles the son of Israel shall die; let them be cast out with stones.

For this law has no appointed time; there is no place for it. He has given his son to idols, and he has called upon God for his own destruction; and concerning all Israel, whoever defiles his son shall be destroyed; there is no forgiveness for him.

And thou, Moses! Command the children of Israel. That they do not mingle with the daughters of the nations, nor let the daughters of the nations mingle with them; for they are set apart before the Lord.
Therefore, concerning the matter of the law, I have written unto you as they of the tribe of Dan did, saying, "For us it is our portion, and we will not give our sister to any man."
To give their daughters to the children of the nations, and to take wives from among the daughters of the nations, for it is a defilement unto Israel, and it is an abomination unto Israel.

If a man takes a wife from among the daughters of the nations, and she bears children to him, Israel shall not be free from this sin. In the matter of the sacrifice, in the matter of the offering, and in the matter of the punishment, all shall come upon him.

If one does this, and sins against these families, and sees not the evil in their eyes, and despises the dwelling of the Lord, and does not regard His glorious name, this sin and all iniquity shall consume the people in unity.
There is no turning back. There is no saying, "I do not see." He shall be accepted as he is, with his offerings and his gifts, and there is no receiving from his hand.
Whether he be a brother or a sister, let it not be that he defiles his body with sin among Israel. Therefore, I have commanded you to bear witness to this matter in Israel.

Concerning what was done to the children of Dan and their sons, as it was given for destruction to the two sons of Jacob, let it be seen that they were consumed without being aware, as they were counted as righteous.

And they, as they were counted as righteous, like the sons of Levi chosen for the priesthood, we in our time have served, and the Levites serve before the Lord as they were chosen. Truly, let him who does righteousness do righteousness, and let him who judges judge, for in Israel, let the Levite be blessed; may his children be blessed forever.

In heaven, let the witnesses be, and to all God, let them present righteousness and blessing thus. While man lives, we shall remember the righteousness he has done. Year by year, at the appointed times, they shall present until a thousand generations. Blessing shall come upon them, and after him, for his children.

In the heavenly scrolls, it is written, "The friend of the Lord is also called a man." I have written all these matters for you. Let them not commit sin, nor let them stray from the law; let them act according to it, and let them write according to it, that they may be the friends of the Lord, and that they may not break the covenant made with Israel's children; I have commanded you to speak this.

Even if they break His covenant, and if all who commit sin act, behold, their adversaries shall be written in the heavenly scrolls; they shall be recorded from the living book; those who perish shall be written in the book in which they are recorded. Even those who perish upon the earth shall be counted with them.

And the sons of Jacob, on the day they perished, acted righteously and did the work of the day, and as for the sinners, they returned as debtors; they were written in the heavenly scrolls. They were also written for a blessing.

They took their sister Dinah from the house of Shechem. They seized all that was in Shechem, all their cattle, all their possessions, and all their wealth, and they brought everything back to their father Jacob.
And there arose from among them the Canaanites and the Perizzites, and they spoke with them because they had destroyed their land.
All the nations surrounding Shechem became the fear of the Lord. For they were struck down by them, and they did not rise to harm the sons of Jacob.
In the month of Abib, Jacob spoke to all his household, saying, "Be clean from sin; and let your garments be changed."
"When I fled from my brother Esau, I was with you; and now let us rise and go to this land in peace, to the Lord, to the place where I prayed to Him, to Bethel."
Among you, let the strangers be put away. Cast away the strange gods that are among you; and whatever is in your ears, and whatever is on your neck, let it be removed."

Rachel took the idols of her father Laban and all her wealth and gave it to Jacob. And he was angered; he broke them; he destroyed them; and they were buried in the land of Shechem, beneath the Jordan.
And in the seventh month, he went up to Bethel. There he made an altar in the place where he had rested. And there he stood in prayer.
And to him, and to the sacrifice, Jacob sent word to his father Isaac; and to his mother Rebekah he sent word.
And Isaac said, “My son Jacob is coming to me; let him not die.”
And Jacob went to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah, and to his father Abraham's house he went.
And among his children, he took both Judah and Levi with him and went to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah.
And Rebekah said, “Behold, your son Jacob has arrived.” And at the sound of this, her heart rejoiced, and she ran from one door to another.

And when she saw both her children, she recognized them. “My son, are these your children?” she asked; and she embraced them. Thus she spoke, saying, “The seed of Abraham shall be honored among you; and you shall be a blessing upon the earth.”
And Jacob entered to his father Isaac to rest. And both his children entered with him.
Holding his father's hand, he approached. And Isaac, leaning upon his son Jacob, blessed him, and his eyes were dimmed with tears.

And he beheld Jacob's two sons, Judah and Levi, and said, “My son, do they resemble you? Are these your children?” And he answered truthfully, “Indeed, they are my children.” He said, “Truly, they are my children.”
ወደ እርሱም ቀረቡ፤ መለስ ብሎም ሁሉን በአንድነት አቅፎ ሳማቸው፤ ትንቢት የሚያናግር መንፈስ ቅዱስ በአፉ አናገረው። ሌዊንም በቀኝ እጁ ያዘው፤ ይሁዳንም በግራ እጁ ያዘ።
በመጀመሪያ ወደ ሌዊ ተመልሶ አስቀድሞ ይመርቀው ጀመር። እንዲህም አለው፥ “እርሱ እግዚአብሔር ይባርክህ፥ የዓለማት ሁሉ ጌታ አንተንና ልጆችህን በዓለሙ ሁሉ ያክብር፤ ክብር ሊሆንህ እግዚአብሔር ለአንተ ገናናነትን ይስጥህ፤ ለልጆችህም ይስጣቸው።

አንተን ወደ እርሱ ያቅርብህ፤ በቤተ መቅደስም ያገለግሉት ዘንድ ከሰው ሁሉ ለይቶ ልጆችህን ወደ እርሱ ያቅርባቸው፤ እንደ መላእክተ ገጽና እንደ ቅዱሳንም እንደ እነርሱ ልጆችህ ለክብር፥ ለጌትነትና ለምስጋና ይሁኑ፤ በዓለሙ ሁሉ ከፍ ከፍ ያድርጋቸው፤ ለያዕቆብም ልጆች ወገኖች ሁሉ መሳፍንትና መኳንንት፥ አለቆችም ይሆናሉ።
የእግዚአብሔርንም ቃል በእውነት ይናገራሉ፤ ፍርዱንም ሁሉ በእውነት ይፈርዳሉ፤ ለያዕቆብ መንገዶችን፥ ለእስራኤልም ፍለጋዬን ይናገራሉ፤ የተወዳጁን ዘር ሁሉ ይመርቁ ዘንድ የእግዚአብሔር በረከት በአፋቸው ይነገራል።
“አንተንም እናትህ ስምህን ሌዊ ብላ ጠራች። ስምህንም በእውነት ጠራች፤ ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር አንድ ትሆናለህ፤ ከያዕቆብ ልጆች ሁሉ ጋር አንድ ትሆናለህ፤ ማዕዱ ለአንተ ትሁን።
አንተና ልጆችህ ብሉአት፤ ማዕድህም ለልጅ ልጅ ሁሉ የመላች ትሁን፤ በዓለሙ ሁሉ እህልህ አይጕደል፤ የሚጠሉህም ሰዎች ሁሉ በፊትህ ይውደቁ፤ ጠላቶችህ ሁሉ ፈጽመው ይጥፉ፤ የሚባርክህ የተባረከ ይሁን፤ የሚረግሙህም ሕዝብ ሁሉ የተረገሙ ይሁኑ።”
ይሁዳንም እንዲህ አለው፥ “የሚጠሉህን ሰዎች ሁሉ ታጠፋቸው ዘንድ እግዚአብሔር ኀይልንና ጽናትን ይስጥህ፤ አንተ ገዥ ሁን፤ ከልጆችህም አንዱ ለያዕቆብ ልጆች ገዥ ይሁን፤ ስምህና የልጆችህ ስም በሀገሩና በከተማው ሁሉ ሲጠራ የሚኖር ይሁን።
ያንጊዜ አሕዛብ ከፊትህ የተነሣ ይፈራሉ፤ አሕዛብም ሁሉ ይታወካሉ፤ ሕዝቡም ሁሉ ይሸበራሉ፤ የያዕቆብ ረድኤት በአንተ ይደር፤ የእስራኤልም ድኅነት በአንተ ትገኛለች።
እውነተኛ ክብር በአለው ዙፋንም በተቀመጥህ ጊዜ ለተወዳጁ ልጆች ዘር ታላቅ ሰላም ይሆናል፤ የሚመርቅህ ሰው የተመረቀ ነው፤ የሚጠሉህና መከራንም የሚያጸኑብህ፥ የሚረግሙህም ሁሉ ከምድር ፈጽመው ይጥፉ፤ የተረገሙም ይሁኑ።”
ዳግመኛ ተመልሶ እቅፍ አድርጎ ሳመው፤ በእውነት የወለዳቸውን የልጁ የያዕቆብን ልጆች አይቶአልና ፈጽሞ ደስ አለው።
And he went forth from between his feet and fell upon the altar, and he blessed them; and he sat beside his father Isaac; and that night they rejoiced greatly and drank.
And he placed the two sons of Jacob, one on his right and the other on his left; and this was counted as righteousness unto him.

And Jacob, the Lord had granted him much forgiveness as he had done, and he declared all the way as he had made it, and he told his father all that he had preserved from every evil thing as it was kept for him that night.
And Isaac, from his servant, the son of Isaac, did not forget his kindness and his forgiveness, and he praised the God of his father Abraham.

And Jacob, when he arose, showed his father Isaac the vision that was given to him, and he also saw the sight, and he prepared the offering as was commanded by God, and all that was to be offered was prepared, and he set it aside to take it as it came.

And Isaac said to his son Jacob, “I have grown old and cannot come forth with you; I cannot walk the way; my son, go in peace, for I am now a man of one hundred and sixty-five years, and thus I cannot go forth.”
“Set your mother aside and go with her; my son, I know that you have come for me; while you are alive, you have seen me, and I have seen you while I am alive; may this day be blessed.”
“My son, prepare yourself and give me your vision; if the vision is delayed, it will be lost in the offering, so do not delay your vision.”
“Now do as you are commanded, that the Lord God who created all may accept your vision with favor.”
And Rebekah said, “Go with your son Jacob.” And Rebekah went with her son Jacob; and Deborah went with her; and they came to Bethel.
And Jacob, seeing his vision, rejoiced, for his father Isaac had separated the offerings of his two sons, Judah and Levi, and he gave thanks to the God of his fathers, the God of Isaac and Abraham.
"Now I know that before the Almighty, there is hope for me forever, and there is hope for my children," he said.
Concerning both, it is thus written: Isaac, as their offering, shall be a witness forever in the heavens; and that night, he was at Bethel.
The Levites, as the chosen ones, served the Most High God, as they were appointed; and their children served as ministers until the end of time, as they were shown in a vision.
And from his sleep, he arose and gave thanks to the Lord. This month, on the twenty-fourth day, Jacob rose early in the morning.
And with him, he brought forth all the tithes, from man to beast, from gold to every other form of wealth, even to clothing, he brought forth all the tithes.
And in those days, Rachel bore her son Benjamin; and Jacob, from him, began to number his children.
He offered a sacrifice; and the sacrifice of the Lord was offered by Levi; and his father put on the garments of the priesthood; and he took his hand.

This month, on the fifteenth day of the month, four goats from the flock, thirty-eight lambs, forty-seven rams, six sheep, and twenty-seven he-goats were offered as a sacrifice to the Lord; and the beloved offering was prepared and brought into the sanctuary before the Lord for a good purpose.
The offering that was brought forth on the day of the feast was this: the offering of the drink was one with it.

And when the fire was kindled, it was customary to place white flour upon the fire. For the burnt offerings, there were four goats, four lambs, four rams, four he-goats, two yearling male goats, and two yearling he-goats that were to be offered. This was done every day for seven days.

And he, along with all his household and his children, rejoiced and feasted for seven days. He gave thanks to the Lord for all that He had delivered him from evil, and he was grateful for all that the Lord had given him. He also brought forth ten clean animals from all the livestock.
And he made the offerings; he gave the unclean animals to his son, to Levi. He also gave of all the offspring of man.
Levi was set apart from his ten brothers, and he ministered before his father Jacob at Bethel.
And there he became a priest; Jacob gave him his offering, and he also gave ten offerings to the Lord. This was sanctified; it was made holy for him.

Therefore, concerning the ten offerings, from year to year, it was to be called by name, that in the chosen holy place, a regular offering before the Lord was to be made, as it was written in the heavenly records.

And for this law, there is no set time for eternity; thus, this ordinance is to be done from year to year, that a regular offering before the Lord in the chosen place is to be made, as it is inscribed in the heavenly records.

The annual feast shall be observed until the time it arrives; thus, it shall be eaten until the year ends; and from this year to the coming year, there shall be no neglect; and until the time it arrives, the wine shall be consumed until the time it arrives, and there shall be no neglect.

Let all that is taken from Him and all that is forsaken be blessed; for it has been blessed and shall be consumed by fire. Thus, let them gather in unity in the house of the sanctuary; let them not be divided.

All the tithes of the herd and of the flock are holy unto the Lord your God. Therefore, concerning the tithes, as it is in heaven, so it shall be upon the earth; let the priests eat before Him from year to year.

On the second night, this month on the fifteenth day, Jacob shall prepare that place, and he shall sanctify it by building an altar; and for him, from everlasting to everlasting, it shall be sanctified for his children until the end of the world.
