And the Lord revealed Himself by night and blessed him, saying: “Your name shall be called Israel, but Jacob shall no longer be called.”
And He said, “I am the Lord your God who created the heavens and the earth; I have honored you, and I have greatly multiplied you.”

The kings shall come forth from you; they shall possess every place; and the sons of men shall possess every place where they have trodden; I shall give you all the nations under heaven for your seed; and as for the peoples, they shall possess them all.

And after this, they shall take hold of all the nations; they shall inherit them forever.” And after He had spoken with him, Jacob departed from Him. And he did not see Him until he ascended to heaven.
And he beheld a vision by night; and behold, an angel descended from heaven; and behold, seven ladders were in his hand.
And He gave to Jacob and revealed to him; He read all that was written within them for his children and for him throughout the world. And He showed him all that was written upon the ladders.

And He said, “Do not make this place a place of worship, nor shall you defile the sanctuary of the everlasting; for this place is not so, and do not come to this place. Go to your father, to the house of Abraham; dwell there until the day your father dies; for while you are in Egypt, you shall die in peace.”

In this land, you shall be received with honor at the tomb of your fathers, alongside Abraham and Isaac; therefore, do not be afraid, for it shall be done as you have seen and as it has been told to you.

"You shall write all that you have seen and all that you have heard." And Jacob said, "How shall I remember all that I have heard and seen?" And the Lord said, "I will cause you to remember all things."
And he arose from there, and Jacob awoke from his sleep; and he remembered all that he had seen and heard. He wrote down all that he had seen and all that he had heard.
And on that day, he made a feast, and he prepared it as it was done in the days of old, and he celebrated. That day was added, and its name was called "The Day of the Feast."
And he called the days of old a feast. And it was so that it was seen thus, for it was written in heaven.

Therefore, concerning the feast that he would make, it was revealed that it should be added to the seven days on which it was celebrated. It is a day of peace, a day of gathering, and it is called "The Day of the Feast."
This month, on the thirtieth day, that night, Deborah, the mother of the children of Israel, died. And they buried her under the oak that is by the city.
And that river was named "The River of Deborah." And the oak was called "The Oak of Deborah."

And Rebekah returned to her father’s house, to the house of Isaac. And Jacob, loving his father, prepared food for him, bringing the delicacies of the goats and the choice meats, and he sent them by her hand.
And he went until he came to the land where his mother was, and he remained there. And there he did.
And Rachel bore a son in the night. And at the time of her giving birth, she was in great distress; therefore she called his name Benoni.

But his father said, "His name shall be Benjamin." In this year of jubilee, in the sixth year, in the first month, on the tenth day of the month, Rachel died. And she was buried in the land which is called Ephrath; this is Bethlehem.
And Jacob set up a pillar upon Rachel's grave, which is the pillar of Rachel's tomb.
And Jacob journeyed toward the south, and he went to his father Isaac along with his wife Leah.
In the tenth month, when Reuben went to gather herbs for his father’s household, he found Rachel's maidservant bathing in the water, and he took her.
And in the night, he entered into the house of his father; and she was found lying alone upon her bed. And when he lay with her, behold, Reuben lay with her and saw her.
And she lifted her hand and cried out; and Reuben knew what had happened. And she arose from him and lifted her hand against him. And he fled. And in this matter, she did not speak to any man.

And Jacob came in the time of his desire, and said, "Because Reuben has wronged me by lying with my wife, I have been separated from you, and I shall not come near you; for I was asleep, and I did not know until I awoke."
"For she has lain with my father, and she has revealed my father's shame," and Jacob was greatly angered against Reuben.
And Reuben was reproached; therefore Jacob did not approach her again. For every man who reveals his father's shame is accursed; for the matter is exceedingly wicked, and it is abominable before God.
ስለዚህ ነገር ሰው ከአባቱ ሚስት ጋር እንዳይተኛ፥ የአባቱንም ኀፍረት እንዳይገልጥ በሰማይ ጽላት ተጽፎአል፤ ርኩስም ስለ ሆነ ሞትን ይሙት።
ከአባቱ ሚስት ጋር የሚተኛ ሰው ጐስቋላ ነው። ሴትም ብትሆን ጐስቋላ ናት። በምድር ርኩስ ሥራን ሠርተዋልና። እርሱም እርስዋም ይሙቱ። በአምላካችን ፊት ለአገዛዝ በመረጠው ወገን መካከል ርኵሰት አይሁን።
ከአባቱ ሚስት ጋር የሚተኛ ሰው የአባቱን ኀፍረት ገልጦአልና የተረገመ ይሆን ዘንድ ዳግመኛ ተጽፎአል።
የእግዚአብሔር ወዳጆች ሁሉ፥ “ይሁን፥ ይሁን” አሉ።
አንተም ሙሴ ይህን ነገር ይጠብቁ ዘንድ የእስራኤልን ልጆች እዘዛቸው፥ ለሞት የሚያበቃ ፍርድ ነውና፥ የረከሰም ነውና።
ይህን ክፉ ሥራ ለሠራ ሰው ከመገደልና በድንጋይ ከመደብደብ፥ ከእግዚአብሔርም ሕዝብ መካከል ተለይቶ ከመጥፋት በቀር በኀጢአቱ ይቅርታና ስርየት የለውም፤ በእስራኤልም መካከል ይህን ሥራ የሚሠራ ማንኛውም ሰው የተናቀና የተጠላ ስለ ሆነ በምድር አንድ ቀን እንኳ መኖር አይገባውም።
ለእርስዋ ባልዋ አባቱ ያዕቆብ በሕይወት ሳለ ከአባቱ ዕቅብት ጋር ከተኛ በኋላ ለሮቤል ሕይወትና ስርየት ነበረው አይበሉ።
በዚያን ጊዜ ለሁሉ ሥርዐትና ሕግ፥ ፍርድም አልተሠራምና፤ ነገር ግን በዘመናችሁ የዘመናትና የቀናት ሕግ እንደ ዘለዓለም ሆኖ ለዘለዓለም ትውልድ ተሠርቶአል።
ለዚህም ሕግ የዘመን ፍጻሜ የለውም። በሕዝቡ መካከል ሁለቱ ሁሉ በአንድነት ይጠፉ ዘንድ፥ ይህችን ኀጢአት በሠሩባት ቀን ይገድሉአቸው ዘንድ ነው እንጂ ለኀጢአታቸው ምንም ስርየት የለውም።
አንተም ሙሴ ለእስራኤል ጻፍላቸው፤ ይጠብቁአት፤ እንደዚህ ያለ ሥራም አይሥሩ፤ ለሞት የሚያበቃ በደልንም አይበድሉ። ፊት አይቶ የማያዳላ፥ መማለጃን የማይቀበል እርሱ አምላካችን እግዚአብሔር እውነተኛ ፈራጅ ነውና።

Hear ye, and keep ye, lest ye be separated from them; for they shall not perish from the earth, but this matter of the law shall be declared unto them. The world, before our Creator, is a great sin unto all who commit it, for it is cast away, it is broken and shattered; and on the earth, there is no greater sin than that which is committed by the dead.

For Israel is a peculiar people unto the Lord God, and a special lineage unto their God, a lineage of priesthood and of kingship; and it is also of wealth. Among the holy people, such a sin ought not to be seen.
And in this sixth month, in the third year, Jacob and his sons went unto their father Isaac and unto their mother Rebekah, and they dwelt in the house of Abraham.

And these are the names of the sons of Jacob: The first is Reuben; the second is Simeon; the third is Levi; the fourth is Judah; the fifth is Issachar; the sixth is Zebulun; these are the sons of Leah.
And the sons of Rachel are Joseph and Benjamin.
And the sons of Bilhah are Dan and Naphtali.
And the sons of Zilpah are Gad and Asher.
Leah bare unto Jacob a daughter, whose name is Dinah. And they went and brought her unto Jacob and unto Rebekah.
And when they beheld, they marveled at Jacob and all his sons. For they saw not the little one, the son of Jacob, and Isaac was greatly pleased at their marveling.
And from this, the fortieth and fourth year, the children of Jacob were sent to tend the sheep in this pasture in the sixth year. And their servants were sent with them to the field of Sekimon.
Under the trees they were gathered, that they might take their wives and their cattle, and the seven kings of the Amorites were gathered against them.

And the children of Jacob, Levi, Judah, and Joseph, were in the house with their father Jacob. For his heart was heavy upon them, and they could not forsake him; therefore, his youngest son Benjamin was with him.
The kings of Tafa, the kings of Aresa, the kings of Selon, the kings of Saragan, the king of Gaez, the king of Bethoron, and the king of Ma'anisikiris, all who dwell in the mountains.
All who dwell under the tree in Canaan came. And to Jacob they said, “Behold, the kings of the Amorites have taken your sons captive; their tents have been uprooted.”
And he arose from his house; and his three sons, all the sons of his father, and his own sons arose.
Nine thousand men bearing weapons went forth and entered the field of Sekimon.
And they followed those who had fled and smote them with the sword; they destroyed Tafa and Aresa, Selon and Saragan, Ma'anisikiris, and Gaez; and they broke their tents.
Upon them was a great height. These five hands brought forth the fruit of their land as tribute, for they wrought tribute upon them.
And he smote Tamina, Taress, and Reuben; and he returned in peace.
And he made peace with them. He and his sons were servants until the day they went down to Egypt.
In this year of the seventh, he sent Joseph from his house to the land of Sekimon, that he might know the welfare of his brethren.
And they found them in the land of Dotaem; and they conspired against him to slay him.

And they returned and sold him to the Ishmaelites. And they brought him down to Egypt, to be a priest for El, a leader for the bread-makers, and they sold him to Pharaoh, to the merchants of Potiphar.
And the sons of Jacob killed a goat and dipped Joseph's coat in the blood.
And the seventh month, on the tenth day, they sent to their father Jacob. And on that day, from morning until evening, they mourned.

And they brought his coat to him; and in the death of his son, he was greatly distressed. They said unto him, "An evil beast hath devoured Joseph." And all the men of his house mourned that day; they wept and lamented with him throughout the day.
And the sons and daughters arose to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted for his son Joseph.
And on that day, he heard that Joseph was dead. And he said, "I shall go down mourning to my son." And she dwelt in her widowhood.
His son Dinah died after Joseph was lost. Upon Jacob, in one month, this sorrow came upon him. And they buried her beside Rachel's tomb; and his daughter Dinah was buried there.
And after the passing of Joseph, a year passed while he mourned. "Concerning my son, concerning Joseph, I shall go down to the grave," he said, and he did not cease his lamentation.

Therefore, on the day when they brought Joseph's robe to his father Jacob, in mourning he commanded that a goat be slaughtered for him, and on the seventh month, on the tenth day, they mourned, and a decree was established upon the children of Israel.
On the tenth day of the seventh month, once a year, because of their sins, they were to be afflicted; for concerning their son, concerning Joseph, their father's heart was grieved.
These days were established for their sins and for all their iniquities; for their transgressions, on this day, once a year, they were to afflict their souls.
And after Joseph was lost, the sons of Jacob took wives for themselves; the name of the wife of the firstborn, Reuben, was Adah.

And the name of the wife of the second, Simeon, was Adinah; she was a woman of Canaan. The name of the wife of the third, Levi, was Milcah; she was born of the daughters of Tarah, of the children of Aram.
The name of the wife of the fourth, Judah, was Bethuel; she was also a woman of Canaan. The name of the wife of the fifth, Issachar, was Hizzah.

The name of the wife of the sixth, Zebulun, was Neamin. The name of the wife of the seventh, Dan, was Eglah. The name of the wife of the eighth, Naphtali, was the woman of Mesopotamia, and she was his own.
The name of the wife of the ninth, Gad, was Mica. The name of the wife of the tenth, Asher, was Iona. The name of the wife of the eleventh, Joseph, was Asenath; she was a woman of Egypt.
The name of the wife of the twelfth, Benjamin, was Iosaka. And Simeon returned and took a second wife from Mesopotamia, like his brothers.

In the fortieth and fifth year of the Jubilee, in the first month, on the first day of the month, Jacob called his son Joseph, and he honored him throughout all the days of his life, for the sake of his brother and for the sake of his father, he commanded him.
And Jacob said, “This matter is for me a honor, for it is also a lordship; and to honor them before God is a good thing, therefore I shall do all that thou hast commanded me.”
My mother, from the day I was born until this day, throughout all my days, I have thought of all good things, and all that is in my heart, thou knowest.

How then shall I not do that which thou hast commanded me, to honor my brother and my father? What evil have I seen in me? My mother, until thou speakest to me; I will indeed depart from him; and let it be that he shall forgive me.”
And she said, “My son, throughout all my days, it is a matter of good work, but there is no evil work that I have seen in thee.”

But, my son! I will speak the truth to thee. This year I shall die. I pray that I may not live beyond fifty years, for the day of my death I cannot bear to see in my dream, and this year I shall not pass in life.”
Behold, all my days that are upon me, I have finished.” Jacob said to his mother, “I shall die,” she said, and concerning her mother she spoke not.

But she was sitting beside him; she was strong; she would go out and come in, for she was seen. Her body was not weak; her teeth were strong; throughout all the days of her life, she did not suffer any sickness.

And Jacob said, “My mother! As for my days in life, as the time draws near, I am indeed weak; my strength, like thine, shall dwell in me; and concerning thy death, thou speakest vain things with me, and thou shalt not die.”

And she said to Isaac, “I have one request I make of thee; thou knowest that the heart of Esau has been evil from his childhood, and there is no goodness in him; after thy death, he will slay me, for he will love Jacob, that he may not do evil to him, and he shall be kept away from him.”

And your brother Jacob, from the time he went to Haran until this day, you know all that he has done in his time; you know that he has acted entirely like a man, and you know that he has done evil against us; he has broken your covenant and taken all your wealth away from you.

He has given us our wealth, for when we lament, he acts like a man who is about to perish; your son Jacob, who is entirely righteous and pure, will surely seek to harm you because of your actions against him.

Except for the goodness, there is no evil; from the time he came from Haran until this day, nothing has harmed us; he has brought us everything in its time, day by day, and when he has received from your hand, his heart has rejoiced entirely; he has honored us; from the time he came from Haran until this day, he has not separated from us.
He has honored us, and he will dwell with us always in the house.
And Isaac said, "He has honored us with all his heart, and I have come to know the work of Jacob that is with us; I do not deny it. From the day he was born, he has loved Esau more than Jacob.
But today, I love Jacob more than Esau. His evil deeds have been multiplied, and there is no good work for him; all his work is deceit and violence, and around him, there is no truth.

Now, concerning all his evil deeds, my heart is troubled. Because of the Creator of Abraham, who followed his wives, and because of their idols, he has followed their errors, and because of their sins, he has been led astray with his children; for him and his descendants, there is no wealth. They are those who will perish from this world beneath the heavens.
But you say, "Do not let your brother Jacob harm him," and you say, "If he is silent, he will not remain in the midst of it; he will not do good works except for evil."
If he desires to harm his brother Jacob, he will fall into Jacob's hand. He will fall by his hand, and he will not be able to escape from his hand.
You said, "Rather than keeping Esau, it is Jacob who is kept, for he is strong and honored, and he is the one who is praised; therefore, do not fear for Jacob."
And Rebekah called unto Esau her son; and he came unto her. And she said, “My son, I have a request of thee; I pray thee, fulfill it for me.”

And he answered her, “I will do all that thou dost ask of me; and I will not withhold thy request.” And she said unto him, “In the time of thy death, let me be buried beside thy father and mother, and let thy brother Jacob and thou be separated from each other.”

And apart from love, let neither one do any evil against his brother, that your children may prosper in your works, and that you may be honored in this world, and that your enemies may not rejoice over you; I beseech thee.
Before all those whom you love, you shall be a source of forgiveness and blessing.”

And he said, “I will do all that thou dost ask of me; and in the time of thy death, let thy bones be laid beside her bones, as I shall bury her beside my father and mother, for I love my brother Jacob more than any man.”
Except for him, I have no other brother upon the earth; for he is my brother, and to love him is not a great matter for me; for in thy womb we were united as one.
For we have come forth from thy womb in unity; and if I do not love my brother, whom shall I love?

Concerning the children and concerning me, I will plead that Jacob be favored; for from the day my father departed, he has been great, and I have been made small; and I know that he shall be favored over me and over my children.
And I, in all the days of my life, will love him, and I shall never wish evil against him, except for good things.
Therefore, concerning all these matters, she commanded that Jacob be called before Esau, that she might speak with him concerning Esau.
እርሱም አላት፥ “እኔ ፈቃድሽን እፈጽማለሁ፤ በወንድሜም በዔሳው ላይ ከእኔና ከልጆች ክፉ ነገር እንደማይወጣ፥ ከፍቅርም በቀር መቼም መች አስቀድሜ እንደማልጣላ ተዋሽኝ።” እርስዋና ልጆችዋም በሉ፤ ጠጡም።
በዚያችም ሌሊት የሦስት ኢዮቤልዩ፥ የአንድ ሱባዔና የአንድ ዓመት ሰው የነበረችው ርብቃ ሞተች። በዚያችም ሌሊት ሁለቱ ልጆችዋ ዔሳውና ያዕቆብ ደርብነት ባላት ዋሻ በአባታቸው እናት በሳራ መቃብር አጠገብ ቀበሩአት።
በዚህ ሱባዔ በስድስተኛው ዓመት ይስሐቅ ሁለቱን ልጆቹን ዔሳውንና ያዕቆብን ጠራቸው፤ ወደ እርሱም መጡ።
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “ልጆች ሆይ! እኔ አባቶች በሄዱበት ጎዳና አባቶች በዚያ ለዘለዓለም ወደሚኖሩበት ቤት እሄዳለሁ፤ አብርሃም ለመቃብር በገዛው፥ እኔ ለራሴ ባስቈፈርሁት፥ በኬጢ ሰው በኤፍሮን እርሻ ውስጥ ባለች ደርብነት ባላት ዋሻ በአባቴ በአብርሃም አጠገብ ቅበሩኝ።”
ልጆች ሆይ! እግዚአብሔር ለአብርሃምና ለዘሩ ያደርግ ዘንድ የነገረውን ሁሉ ለእናንተ እንዲያደርግላችሁ በዚህ ዓለም እውነትንና ቅንነትን ትሠሩ ዘንድ ይህን አዘዝኋችሁ።
ልጆች ሆይ! ሰው ራሱን እንደሚወድድ እርስ በርሳችሁ ወንድሞቻችሁን እየወደዳችሁ ኑሩ።
ሰው ለወንድሙ በጎ ነገርን ያደርግለት ዘንድ ፈልጎ፥ ይህንም በምድር ላይ በልቡናው በአንድነት አድርጎ፥ እርስ በርሳቸው እንደ ራሳቸው እንደሚፋቀሩ፥ እርስ በርሳችሁ የምትፋቀሩ ሁኑ።
ስለ ጣዖቱም ነገር ትንቁአቸውና ትጠሉአቸው ዘንድ፥ እንዳትወዱአቸውም እኔ አዝዛችኋለሁ። ለሚያመልኳቸውና ለሚሰግዱላቸው ሰዎች ስሕተትን የተመሉ ናቸውና፤
ልጆች ሆይ፥ የአባታችሁን የአብርሃምን አምላክ እግዚአብሔርን ዐስቡት።
ከዚህም በኋላ እኔ አመለክሁት። በእውነትና በሰፊ ልቡና ተገዛሁለት። በደስታ ያበዛችሁ ዘንድ፥ ልጆቻችሁንም እንደ ሰማይ ኮከብ ለማብዛት ያሳድግላችሁ ዘንድ፥ ለዘለዓለም ትውልድም ሁሉ የማይነቀል የእውነተኛ ተክል አድርጎ በምድር ይተክላችሁ ዘንድ ዐስቡት።

"Now I declare unto you, O my God, in great majesty. There is none greater than He, who is praised, honored, and revered, who is mighty and strong, who created the heavens and the earth, and who holds all things together. In the name of the Lord God, there is no greater majesty than this; each one of you should fear and honor your brother with forgiveness and kindness, as I declare unto you."
"From this day forth, even unto eternity, in all the days of your life, that you may be diligent in all your works, let no man do evil against his brother."
"If there be any man who desires to do evil against his brother, let him know that he shall fall like a stone from his hand, and like the earth that is alive, from this day forth, he shall perish."

"On the day when strife, wrath, and anger shall be stirred up, the heavens shall be shaken, and this world shall perish; and the Lord shall consume it with the fire that He kindles, as He destroyed Sodom, so shall He consume the land and the city. All that is His wealth shall be consumed; the deeds of the son of man shall be blotted out from the book in which they are written."

"For He is the one who shall perish, and for eternity, He shall be cast away; in all his days, his wickedness shall be revealed, and in sorrow and wrath, in the eternal day of judgment, he shall not be written in the book of life."
"Children, behold, as punishment comes upon the man who does evil against his brother, so shall I speak unto you, and I shall admonish you."
"On that day, all the wealth that exists shall be given to both of them; and honor shall be given beforehand to the son who is born. He gave the foundation and all that is around it."
"Abraham gave all the wealth that he had acquired to his son; and he said, 'I have given this great honor beforehand to the son who is born.'"
"And Esau said, 'I have sold my birthright to Jacob; let him receive the honor that pertains to my birthright; for he is my brother, and concerning her, I have nothing to say.'"

"And Isaac said, 'Children, do not provoke me, for I have not grieved because of her; and on this day, may blessings come upon you and your children; may the Lord bless the one who does good works; may He bless him and his seed forever.'"
ይህን አዝዞአቸውና መርቆአቸው ከጨረሰ በኋላ በፊቱ በአንድነት በሉ፤ ጠጡም።
በመካከላቸውም መተካከል ሆኖአልና ደስ አላቸው። ከእርሱም ዘንድ ወጡ፤ በዚያችም ቀን ዐርፈው ተኙ።
ይስሐቅም ደስ ብሎት በዚያች ቀን በአልጋው ላይ ተኛ፤ የዘለዓለምንም እንቅልፍ አንቀላፋ።
የመቶ ሰማንያ ዐመት ሰው ሆኖ ሞተ። ሃያ አምስት ሱባዔንና አምስት ዓመትን ጨረሰ። ሁለቱ ልጆቹ ዔሳውና ያዕቆብም ቀበሩት።
ዔሳውም በኤዶምያስ አውራጃ ወደ አለች ወደ ሴይር ተራራ ሄደ፤ በዚያም ኖረ።
ያዕቆብም አባቱ አብርሃም ተሰዶ ይኖርበት በነበረ በኬብሮን ምድር ባለ ግንብ ኖረ።
እንደ ተወለደበት ወራት እንደሚታየው ትእዛዝ አድርጎ በፍጹም ልቡናው እግዚአብሔርን አመለከው።
በአርባ አምስተኛው ኢዮቤልዩ በሁለተኛው ሱባዔ በአራተኛው ዓመት ሚስቱ ልያ ሞተች። በአባቱ እናት በሳራ መቃብር በስተግራ በእናቱ በርብቃ መቃብር አጠገብ ደርብነት በአላት ዋሻ ቀበራት።
ልጆቹና ልጆችዋ ሁሉ ለሚስቱ ለልያ ከእርሱ ጋር ያለቅሱላት ዘንድ፥ ስለ እርስዋም ያረጋጉት ዘንድ መጡ፤ ያለቅስላት ነበርና። በሥራዋም ሁሉ ፈጽማ ቅን ስለሆነች እኅቷ ራሔል ከሞተች ጀምሮ ፈጽሞ ይወድዳት ነበርና።
ያዕቆብንም ታከብረው ነበር፤ ከእርሱም ጋር በኖረችበት ዘመን ሁሉ ክፉ ነገር ከአፍዋ አልሰማም፤ የዋህና ሰላማዊት ነበረችና፥ ሰላም፥ ቅንነት፥ ክብርም ያላት ነበረችና።
While she was alive, she used to think upon all her works; she was without blemish. For she loved him with her whole body and with her whole heart.
On the day when Isaac, the father of Esau and Jacob, passed away, the sons of Esau heard that Isaac had blessed Jacob, his younger son, as he had given him the blessing.
And they spoke, saying, “You are great, while Jacob is your younger brother; why did your father give the blessing to Jacob instead of you?” Thus they contended with their father.
And he said unto them, “I sold my birthright for a small morsel of food; therefore, this is the reason.”
And I brought forth to my father what he had sent me to bring, and I presented to my father that which he would eat and drink. And my father was pleased; and he made me to be beneath him.
Now, let us not engage in evil with our brother; rather, let us dwell with love and peace with our brother, that we may not cause our paths to be lost, for our fathers have united me and him.

And they said, “You do not desire to make peace with him; for his strength will prevail over our strength, and we will be weakened before him, and we will go against him; and we will go against his children; and if you do not go with us, we will do evil against you.”
Now, let us choose for ourselves chosen men to go to Aram, to Philistia, to Ammon, and to Moab, who will be sent to us in ambush.
And let us go against him, and let us contend with him; and let us not be weakened from the earth.
And their father said unto them, “Do not go; and do not let your faces be hidden from him; keep watch and do not act wickedly against him.”
And they said, “From your childhood until this day, is your work only this? You will surely be brought to the tent; we do not hear this matter.”
And they agreed with him to send a thousand men, chosen from the Arameans and from their fathers, and from the friends of Aduram, to slay them.
A thousand warriors chosen from the children of Ammon and Moab,
A thousand warriors chosen from the Philistines,
A thousand warriors chosen from Edom and from Korah,
And from Keteon came strong warriors, and they came to him.
And they said to their father, “Go forth and lead them; if this is not so, we shall lead you.” And he went to his brother Jacob to lead them, and his sons were filled with anger at the sight.
And after this, he harbored in his heart all the wickedness against his brother Jacob. Nevertheless, in all his days, he did not think of speaking ill of his brother Jacob to his mother and father.

But Jacob did not know all this, that they were coming to fight against him. And he remained with the chosen four thousand warriors and soldiers until they drew near to him, and he was troubled for his wife Leah.
And the men of Hebron said, “Behold, your brother is coming to fight against you, having drawn his sword, and with his shield and his weapons, he came with four thousand men,” and they sent to him.

For Jacob was loved more than Esau; thus it was said: "Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents," and he was indeed more virtuous than Esau. And Jacob did not believe what was said until he drew near to the door of the tent.
And he stood by the door of the tent and spoke with his brother Esau, saying, "Did you come to me to comfort me because my wife has died?"
Is this not the truth that you hastened to come, before your father and mother have died?
"You have come to me with evil intent; and at the time of your father's blessing, you were deceived." And Esau answered him at that time.
Thus he said, "There is no true blessing upon the earth for beasts and for the children of men that shall endure forever."
Each day, this seeks to bring forth strife. Each one desires to slay his adversary.

You too shall be an adversary to me until the end of days; there shall be no brotherhood between you and me. Hear this word that I speak unto you. If you should change your countenance and your appearance as a wolf,
as a goat, should you come forth with your own skin, then I shall establish brotherhood with you.

If the teeth should be separated from the mothers, I was indeed a brother. And if they should not devour one another and should not harm one another, if they should dwell in peace with the goats, and their hearts should think to do good unto them,

then in that moment, in my heart, there shall be peace towards you. If a lion should be a friend to a lamb, and if they should lie down together in one fold, and if they should be at peace with one another, then in that moment, I shall establish peace with you.
"When the quails fall like the saplings, at that time, as I have made peace with you, I know that you shall perish, and your children shall also perish. Peace shall not be made for you."
"And at that time, Jacob, having troubled his heart, he was indeed aware that he was being slain by his own heart."
"As a man flees swiftly from the sword that is drawn against him, so Esau came swiftly, as one who does not flee from him."
"At that time, he commanded all his servants, and his kindred, and all his friends to be gathered."

"And after this, Judah spoke to his father Jacob, saying, 'My father, behold, your garment is torn, and your son is in distress; let your distress be upon me; let your distress be upon me, and may strength be given to you.'"
"We shall not slay your brother; for he is with you, and we are to honor him as you do."
"And at that time, Jacob took his garment, and his distress was upon him, and he slayed his brother Esau."
"And he also took the distress of the people, and he became a leader of the tribes, and he smote the left breast of the adversary; he also smote him."
And after this, the sons of Jacob, along with their servants, went forth into the wilderness, by the four corners of the earth.
Judah went forth first; and with him were Naphtali and Gad, and fifty men of the Belaites. They smote all that they encountered before them. Among them, there was not a single man who escaped.
Levi, Dan, and Asher went forth into the eastern wilderness; and fifty men of the Belaites were with them. They smote the adversaries of Moab and Ammon.
Reuben, Issachar, and Zebulun went forth into the northern wilderness; and fifty men of the Belaites were with them; they smote the Philistine warriors.

Simeon, Benjamin, and the son of Reuben, Enoch, went forth into the western wilderness; and fifty men of the Belaites were with them. They smote four hundred mighty men from Edom and Korah. However, six hundred of them fled; and four were the sons of Esau.
Their father died upon the mountain, as they fled from him, like a fallen leaf. This is the mountain that is in Aduram; and the sons of Jacob pursued them until they reached the mountain of Seir.

But Jacob returned to his house, having buried his brother in the mountain of Aduram. The sons of Jacob distressed the sons of Esau in the mountain of Seir. And for the sons of Jacob, they became their enemies, so they lowered their necks.
And they were to make peace with them, as it was, and they sent them to their father.
And Jacob sent peace to his sons; and they made peace with them.
In all their days, let them be honored for Jacob and his sons, and let the banner of their victory rest upon them.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of Egypt until the day he departed; and the children of Edom, even the twelve sons of Jacob, were not oppressed by them in the service of tribute until that day.
Until that day, there was no king over the children of Israel, and these are the kings who reigned in Edom.
In Edom reigned Balaq, the son of Zippor; and the name of the city was Dinhabah; and Balaq died.
And in his stead reigned Jobab, the son of Zerah, from Bozrah. And Jobab, the son of Zerah, died. And in his stead reigned Husham, from the land of Teman; and Husham died.
And in his stead reigned Hadad, the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab; and the name of the city was Avith. And Hadad died.

And in his stead reigned Samlah, from Masrekah; and Samlah died. And in his stead reigned Saul, from Rehoboth by the river; and Saul died. And in his stead reigned Baal-hanan, the son of Achbor; and Baal-hanan, the son of Achbor, died.
And in his stead reigned Hadad; and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.
And Jacob, his father, was a wanderer in the land where he sojourned; and Jacob dwelt in the land of Canaan.
And Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and they sold him into Egypt after they had stripped him.
And by reason of Joseph, the blessing of the Lord was upon the house of the Egyptian; and the Lord blessed all that he did.
And the Egyptian man saw that the Lord was with Joseph, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand; and he was favored in the sight of all.
Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance, and he was greatly admired.

And the wife of his master cast her eyes upon Joseph, and she said, "Lie with me." But he refused, and said to his master's wife, "Behold, my master does not know what is with me in the house, and he has committed all that he has to my hand."

And he thought upon God, and he remembered the words of his father Abraham, that no man should lie with a woman who is married; and he thought upon the punishment of death that is ordained in the sight of the Lord for such a deed. In all his days, he thought of the sin against God, as it is written in the book of the everlasting.
And Joseph considered this matter; he did not desire to lie with her, for he had been with her for a year; he did not listen to her voice.
But she was determined to lie with him, and she troubled him in the house; she seized his garment, and he fled from her presence, leaving his garment in her hand.
And when she saw that he had fled from her, she spoke in the presence of her lord, saying, "This Hebrew servant whom you have brought to us came in to me to mock me."
And thus it was, that when I lifted my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled.
And the Egyptian saw Joseph's garment that was torn.
And when she spoke concerning him to her husband, he was enraged, and he cast Joseph into the prison where the king's prisoners were confined.

And he dwelt there in the prison. And the Lord gave Joseph favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison, and he gave him mercy before him. The Lord was with him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hand.
Joseph was in charge of all things, and the Lord was with him, so that the keeper of the prison knew nothing that he had in his hand.

And it came to pass in those days that Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, was angry with his two officers, the chief butler and the chief baker. And Joseph was bound in the prison, and he was in charge of the prisoners.
The chief of the prisoners spoke to them, saying, "Tell me your dreams," and he interpreted their dreams.
Both the chief butler and the chief baker had dreams. They told Joseph, and he interpreted them according to their dreams.
And Pharaoh restored the chief butler to his position, as Joseph had interpreted, but he hanged the chief baker.
The chief butler, however, forgot Joseph in the prison. Joseph had been speaking to Pharaoh, but he did not remember him. He remained forgotten.
And in those days, Pharaoh beheld two dreams in one night, concerning the calamity and famine that would come upon all the land.
And he awoke from his sleep; and he called for all the magicians and wise men that were in Egypt, and he told them his dreams. But they could not interpret them.
After this, the chief butler remembered Joseph; and he spoke of him to the king.
They brought him out of the prison, and he spoke to them both concerning their dreams.
And he said unto them, "The two dreams are one," and he declared them before Pharaoh.
He said, "Behold, there shall come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt; and after them shall arise seven years of famine, such as there hath not been in all the land."

Now, all the people of Egypt shall gather unto Pharaoh for food; during the time of famine, the grain that is found in the land shall be for food; for the seven years of famine that shall come, there shall be food; and the famine shall be very grievous, so that the land shall not perish from the famine."
And the Lord gave Joseph favor and mercy in the sight of Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said unto his servants, "Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?"

And in his kingdom, he appointed another man; and he made him overseer over all the land of Egypt; and he set him over the second chariot which he had; and he clothed him in fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

"El El Abir" he spoke before him; and he made for him a golden chain upon his hand; and he adorned his house; he made it high and lifted up. And he said, "Except for the throne, I shall not be greater than you."

And Joseph was made ruler over all the land of Egypt; and all the princes of Pharaoh and all his servants loved him; for he was found to be a man of integrity, and there was no pride in him, nor was there any deceit, and he did not seek to take advantage of others. He judged all the peoples of Egypt justly.

And the land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph. For the Lord was with him. In all the days of Pharaoh's reign, among all the people who knew him, he was a witness of integrity and mercy. And the kingdom of Pharaoh was prosperous. There was no evil in it.
And the king called Joseph, saying, "Sephanath-Paneah." He gave him as a wife the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be a companion to Joseph.
And Joseph stood before Pharaoh, and he was a man of thirty years.
And in that year, Isaac died. Concerning the two dreams, the interpretation that Joseph had spoken came to pass.
In all the land of Egypt, there were seven years of famine; and the land of Egypt produced much fruit; one measure was worth eight hundred measures.
And Joseph, until the harvest was complete, gathered the grain; and he counted it until they were satisfied, and he gathered the food of the city from all the lands.
In the forty-fifth jubilee, in the second year, Judah took a wife for his firstborn, Er, from the daughters of Aram; her name was Tamar.
And a rival, she did not sleep with her; for her mother was a Canaanite; and to take a wife from his mother's family, he desired; yet his father Judah did not permit him.
And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was wicked in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord slew him.
Then Judah said to his son Onan, “Go in unto your brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up seed to your brother.”

But Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother’s wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother. And the thing which he did displeased the Lord; therefore He slew him also.

Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow at your father’s house till Shelah my son be grown; for he said, ‘Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren did.’” And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.
And in the process of time the daughter of Shuah, Judah’s wife, died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheep shearers to Timnath; he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
And it was told Tamar, saying, “Behold, your father-in-law goes up to Timnath to shear his sheep.”

And she put her widow’s garments off from her, and covered her with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.

When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; because she had covered her face. And he turned unto her by the way, and said, “Go to, I pray you, let me come in unto you.” For he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me, that you may come in unto me?”

And he said, “I will send you a kid from the flock.” And she said, “Will you give me a pledge, till you send it?” And he said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your signet, and your bracelets, and your staff that is in your hand.” And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose, and went away, and laid by her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

And Judah, having sent away the harlot, asked the men of the place, saying, "Where is the harlot that was in this place?" And they said, "There is no harlot in this place, nor has there been one among us."
And he returned, saying, "I asked the men of the place, and they said to me, 'There is no harlot in this place.'"

And he said, "Let us arise and go to our business." And after three months, she was discovered to be with child; and it was told to Judah, saying, "Behold, your daughter-in-law has played the harlot; she is with child by whoredom."
And Judah went to his father's house and said to his father and his mother and his brethren, "She has committed a great sin in Israel, and let her be brought forth to be burned."

And it came to pass, when they brought her forth to be burned, that she sent to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man whose these are, I am with child." And she said, "Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and the bracelets, and the staff."
And Judah said, "She is more righteous than I, forasmuch as I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he knew her again no more.
And after she had borne him, in the second year of the second sabbatical cycle, she bore two sons, Perez and Zerah.
And after this, the thing that Joseph spoke to Pharaoh was fulfilled; the seven years of famine came to pass.

And Judah was joined to his daughter-in-law, and he knew that what he had done was evil. He uncovered his own shame before his eyes. And he revealed the wickedness of his son, and he knew that he had done wrong, as it was evil and as it was shameful.
Concerning the wickedness, let us be seized before the Lord and let us begin to repent.

Truly, concerning the dream, it was said that he should be punished for his transgression. After this, sin shall not be committed. He has returned from his sin and from the knowledge of the world, and he has become a reproach.

Before our God, it is written: "Every man who does such things, and every man who lies with his daughter-in-law, shall be burned with fire. For they have become sin and iniquity, and therefore they shall be burned with fire."

And you shall say, "Let not the children of Israel be defiled with abominations; for every man who lies with his daughter-in-law has committed abomination, and he shall be burned with fire along with the woman with whom he lies."
His wrath and his anger shall be poured out upon Israel.
And concerning Judah, his two sons were not to be with her; therefore, his seed became for another purpose.
For his children, from the command of Abraham, Judah shall be burned with fire, and he has been loved, and he has walked in righteousness, and he has not forsaken judgment.
In the forty-fifth year, the jubilee began in the third month; in the first year, the earth began to yield abundantly.

And the rain was upon the earth, and it ceased. There was no descent, for the earth was barren. But in the land of Egypt, there was food; for in the year of abundance, Joseph had gathered the grain of Egypt and kept it.
And the people of Egypt came to Joseph to receive their food. And he opened the storehouses of grain for the people of his country and sold it to them for gold during the first year of famine.
And Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt. He sent his ten sons to buy grain from Egypt.

But he did not send Benjamin. And they came to the man who was in charge of the land of Egypt. And Joseph recognized them; but they did not recognize him. And he spoke to them, saying, "Are you not spies? You have come to see the nakedness of the land."
After this, he imprisoned them; and he only kept Simeon. He filled their sacks with grain and returned their money to them; but they did not know it.
Their father was still alive, and their younger brother was still alive, so he commanded them to bring their younger brother.

And they departed from the land of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan; and they told their father all that had happened to them, saying, "The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and took Simeon from us until Benjamin returns."
And Jacob said to them, "You have bereaved me; Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you will take Benjamin away? All these things are against me."

And their mother had borne them two sons, and one of them died; and will you take this one away? If he should die on the way, you would bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave." And all their goods were returned to them, and he feared to send him.

Many people of Egypt came to Joseph, for he was gathering much grain, and he was storing it for the years of famine. Thus, he provided food for them, and in all the land of Canaan, the famine was severe.
And the people of Egypt gathered in the first year of famine.
ያዕቆብም በምድር ረኃብ እጅግ እንደ ጸና፥ መዳንም እንደ ሌለ ባየ ጊዜ ልጆቹን፥ “እንዳንሞት ወደ ግብፅ ሄዳችሁ እህል ሸምታችሁ አምጡልን” አላቸው። እነርሱም፥ “ታናሹ ወንድማችን ከእኛ ጋር ካልሄደ አንሄድም” አሉት።
ያዕቆብም ብንያምን ከእነርሱ ጋር ካልሰደደው ከራቡ የተነሣ ሁሉም እንደሚጠፉ ዐሰበ፥ ሮቤልም፥ “እርሱን በእጄ ስጠኝ፤ መልሼ ባላመጣልህ ስለ እርሱ ፋንታ ሁለቱን ልጆችን ግደላቸው” አለው።
እርሱም፥ “ከአንተ ጋር አይሄድም” አለው። ይሁዳም ቀርቦ፥ “ከእኔ ጋር ስደደው፤ መልሼ ባላመጣልህም በሕይወት ዘመኔ ሁሉ በፊትህ በደለኛ ልሁን” አለ።
በዚህ ሱባዔ በሁለተኛው ዓመት በዐሥረኛው ወር መባቻ ከእነርሱ ጋር ሰደደው፤ ከሚሄዱትም ሁሉ ጋር ወደ ግብፅ ደረሱ። ከእነርሱም ጋር እጅ መንሻቸው ልባንጃ፥ ለውዝ፥ ጠርቤንቶስና የማር ወለላ በእጃቸው ነበር።
ደርሰውም በዮሴፍ ፊት ቆሙ። ወንድሙን ብንያምንም ባየው ጊዜ ዐወቀው።
“ትንሽ ወንድማችሁ ይህ ነውን?” አላቸው። እነርሱም፥ “አዎን፥ ነው” አሉት። እርሱም፥ “ልጄ ሆይ፥ እግዚአብሔር ይጠብቅህ” አለው፥ ወደ ቤቱም ሰደዳቸው፤ ስምዖንንም አወጣላቸው።
ግብርም አገባላቸው፥ በእጃቸውም ያመጡትን እጅ መንሻቸውን አቀረቡለት። በፊቱም በሉ፤ ለሁሉም ፋንታ ፋንታቸውን ሰጣቸው። ከሁሉም ፋንታ ይልቅ የብንያም ፋንታ ሰባት እጅ በለጠ። በሉ፥ ጠጡም፥ ሄደውም አህዮቻቸው ባሉበት ዐደሩ።
ዮሴፍም እርስ በርሳቸው የደኅንነትና የሰላም ዐሳብ እንዳላቸው፥ ያም ባይሆን የጠብ ዐሳብ እንዳላቸው፥ ዐሳባቸውን ያውቅ ዘንድ ዐሰበ።
በቤቱ ላይ የተሾመውንም ሹም፥ “በአቅማዳቸው ሁሉ እህልን ምላላቸው፥ ወርቃቸውንም በየአቅማዳቸው አድርግላቸው፤ የምጠጣበትንም የብሩን ጽዋ በታናሹ ልጅ አቅማዳ አድርገህ ስደዳቸው” አለው።
እርሱም ዮሴፍ እንዳዘዘው አደረገ። በየአቅማዳውም እህሉን ሁሉ መላ፥ ወርቃቸውንም በየአቅማዳቸው ጨመረላቸው። የብሩንም ጽዋ በብንያም አቅማዳ ጨመረ፤ በነጋም ጊዜ ፈጥነው ሄዱ።
ከዚያም በወጡ ጊዜ እንዲህ ሆነ። ዮሴፍ በቤቱ የተሾመውን ሹም፥ “ፈጥነህ ተከተላቸው፦ በጎ ነገርን ስላደረግሁላችሁ ፋንታ ክፉ ነገር ከፈላችሁኝ፤ ጌታዬም የሚጠጣበትን የብር ጽዋ ሰረቃችሁኝ ብለህ ተከራክረህ ታናሽ ወንድማቸውን መልስልኝ፥ ወደ አደባባይ ሳልወጣ ፈጥነህ አምጣው” አለው።
በኋላቸውም ፈጥኖ ተከትሎ እንዲህ ባለ ነገር ተናገራቸው። እነርሱም አሉት፥ “ለእኛ ለባሪያዎችህ እንዲህ ያለ ነገር አግባባቸው አይደለም። ይህን ነገር አያደርጉም፤ ከጌታህም ቤት ምንም ገንዘብ አይሰርቁም።
እኛ ባሪያዎችህ ቀድሞ በአቅማዳችን ያገኘነውን ወርቃችንን ስንኳ ከከነዓን መልሰናል፥ እንዴት ገንዘብ እንሰርቃለን? እነሆ፥ እኛም አለን፤ አቅማዳችንም አለ፤ በርብር።
ከእኛም ጽዋውን ያገኘህበት አንዱ ሰው ይገደል፤ እኛም አህዮቻችንም ለጌታህ እንገዛ።”
እርሱም አላቸው፥ “ነገሩ እንዲህ አይደለም፤ ጽዋውን ያገኘሁበትን ሰው እርሱን ብቻ ይዤ አገልጋይ አደርገዋለሁ፤
እናንተ ግን በሰላም ወደ ቤታችሁ ተመለሱ።”
ገንዘባቸውንም ሲበረብር ከትልቁ ጀምሮ በታናሹ ጨረሰ፤ በታናሹም በብንያም አቅማዳ ተገኘ። ደንግጠውም ልብሶቻቸውን ቀደዱ። አህዮቻቸውንም ጭነው ወደ ከተማ ተመለሱ። ወደ ዮሴፍም ቤት ደረሱ። ሁሉም በግንባራቸው በምድር ላይ ተደፍተው ሰገዱለት።
And Joseph said unto them, "Ye have done evil unto me." And they said, "What shall we say? How shall we answer? Thou, our lord, hast found the iniquity of thy servants upon us;
Behold, we are servants unto our lord; and our asses are also his."

And Joseph said unto them, "I fear God; and ye shall go unto your land, for ye have done wickedly, and let your brother be the only one to remain; as a man loveth his own soul, so shall I drink from this cup. Do ye not know that ye have wronged me?"

And Judah said, "My lord, let thy servant speak a word in thine ears. This thy servant's mother bore two sons unto our father; and one went away and is lost; and he is not found. But this one, behold, he remaineth with his mother alone."

Thy servant's father loveth him; and his heart is bound up with the heart of this child. If we go back to thy servant, our father, and this child be not with us, he will die; for his soul is knit with the soul of this child.

Until death, we shall bring grief upon our father. Yet I, thy servant, will be a surety for this child unto my lord; and let him go with his brethren. For I shall bring him back to our father, and I will bear the blame forever.
And Joseph saw that their hearts were united in good, and he could not refrain himself any longer.
And he spake unto them, and he spoke in the Hebrew tongue, and he made himself known unto them. And he wept aloud, and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard.

And he said unto them, "Do not be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, for ye sold me hither; for God did send me before you to preserve life. For these two years hath the famine been in the land, and yet there are five years in which there shall neither be plowing nor harvest."
Many shall come to seek help, for the Lord hath sent me before you to prepare a way. And I am still alive; tell my father of my life."
ለፈርዖን እንደ አባቱ እሆን ዘንድ፥ በቤቱና በግብፅ ሀገርም ሁሉ እሠለጥን ዘንድ እግዚአብሔር እንደ ሾመኝ እነሆ፥ እናንተ ታያላችሁ።
ለአባቴም፦ ጌትነቴን ሁሉ፥ እግዚአብሔርም የሰጠኝን ብልጽግናና ክብርን ሁሉ ንገሩት።”
በፈርዖንም ትእዛዝ ለመንገድ ሰረገላዎችንና ስንቅን ሰጣቸው። ለሁሉም አራት ኅብር ያለው ልብስና ብርን ሰጣቸው። ለአባታቸውም ልብስና ብርን፥ ስንዴ የሚወስዱባቸውንም ዐሥር አህዮች ላከ። አሰናበታቸውም።
ወጥተውም ለአባታቸው፥ ዮሴፍ በሕይወት እንደ አለ፥ በምድር ላሉ አሕዛብ ሁሉ ስንዴን እንደሚሰፍር፥ በግብፅ ሀገር ሁሉም ላይ እንደ ሠለጠነ ነገሩት።
አባታቸው ግን ልቡናው ደንግጦአልና አላመናቸውም።
ከዚህ በኋላ ዮሴፍ የላከለትን ሰረገላዎች አይቶ ሰውነቱ እንደ ገና ታደሰ።

Let it remain, or let it descend, that which is seen as it is; thus, on that seventh day, it was established. And from the harvest, he made the feast of the first fruits.
For among the beasts and the cattle, among the birds and all men, since it was unclean, there was no full seed that was found in the land of Canaan.

And on the thirty-sixth day, the Lord appeared and called, “Jacob, Jacob.” And Jacob said, “Here I am.” And He said, “I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will do much for you, and do not fear to go down to Egypt; for I will go down with you. I will also bring you up, and there you shall be buried.”
And Joseph shall place his hand upon your eyes; do not fear; and go down to Egypt.”
And Jacob arose; and his sons and his sons' sons arose; they loaded their father and their wives upon the wagons.
And in this third month, on the thirty-sixth day, Jacob arose from the land of Canaan and went down to Egypt.
And Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to direct his face to Goshen; and they came to the land of Egypt to dwell there, for Joseph had commanded them.
And it was good in the land of Egypt. And it was near to him, and it was pleasing to Israel and to his cattle.

These are the names of the sons of Jacob who went down to Egypt with their father Jacob. The firstborn of Jacob is Reuben. And the names of his sons are Enoch, Phallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these five are with him.
Simeon and his sons; and the names of his sons are these: Imuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman; these seven are with him.
The sons of Levi, and these are their names: Gershon, Kohath, Merari, these are the four.
The sons of Judah, and these are their names: Shelah, Perez, Zerah, these are the four.
The sons of Issachar, and these are their names: Tola, Puah, Jashub, Shimron, these are the five.
The sons of Zebulun, and these are their names: Sered,

The sons of Jacob, and these are their sons: these are they; six were born to Leah, who bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia. One of them is their sister, Dinah. All the children born to Leah went down to Egypt with their father Jacob, numbering thirty and nine. Their father Jacob was joined to them and became forty.
The sons of Jacob's wife Zilpah, whom she bore to Jacob, are Gad and Asher. Their children who went down to Egypt with them are these.
The sons of Gad are Zephon, Haggi,
And the sons of Asher are Imnah, Ishvah, Beriah; and their sister was Serah. These are the five.
The sons of Zilpah are fourteen. All the sons of Leah are forty and four.

The sons of Jacob's wife Rachel are Joseph and Benjamin. Their father went not down to Egypt, but to Joseph were born in Egypt. The sons of the priest Elihoenai, who is of the family of Phinehas, are Manasseh and Ephraim. These are the three.

The sons of Benjamin are: Bela, Becher, and Jediah, three; and the sons of Bela were: Ezbon, Uzzi, and the sons of Jediah were: Bilhan and the sons of Becher were: Nahath, Ahijah, and the sons of Jediah were: Bilhan and the sons of Becher were: Nahath, Ahijah, and the sons of Jediah were: Bilhan.
And these are the children of Dan and Naphtali, whom the wife of Jacob, Rachel's maid, bore. And with them went down into Egypt the names of their children.
The children of Dan are: Hushim, Shuham, and the sons of Dan are six. They died in the year they entered Egypt. Only Hushim was left for Dan.

And these are the names of the children of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem; and they were born after the time of the captivity in Egypt. All the people of Rachel were seventy, and all the children of Jacob who went down into Egypt were seventy souls.
Thus, these are the sons and the sons of their sons, all seven. And the wives who died in Egypt were five; and there were no sons among them.
The two sons of Judah were Er and Onan, who died in the land of Canaan, and they had no sons; and they buried the dead of the children of Israel. And these clans were counted with the seven men.
And Jacob entered the land of Egypt in the forty-fifth year, in the third month, in the second year, in the fourth month.
And Joseph received his father Jacob and came into the land of Goshen. And he embraced his father and wept. And Jacob said to Joseph, “I can die now, for I have seen your face.”

“Now, from my servant Jacob, may the mercy and forgiveness of the God of Israel, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac be praised; for the vision I saw at Bethel is indeed a true dream, and seeing you alive is a great thing for me; may my God, the Lord, be praised forever; His name is blessed,” he said.

And Joseph and his brothers said before their father, “Let us eat bread;” and they drank wine. And Jacob saw Joseph eating and drinking with his brothers and was filled with joy. He praised the one who kept him, the twelve sons, and thanked the Creator of all.
And Joseph also gave money to his father, and he provided for his brothers, that they might dwell in the land of Goshen and in the region of Rameses before Pharaoh.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of Egypt with his children, in the land of Goshen. And when Jacob entered into Egypt, he was a man of one hundred thirty years.
And Joseph provided food for his father and for his brothers, and for their households, enough for the years of famine. And the land of Egypt was made desolate because of the famine.
And Joseph made all the land of Egypt serve Pharaoh for grain, and he gathered money for Pharaoh from the people, both man and beast. And the years of famine were fulfilled.

In the seventh year of the famine, Joseph gave seed and food to the people of Egypt. The river returned in the land of Egypt, and in the seven years of famine, there was no water except in a few places.
But today the river has returned; the people of Egypt have sown the land, and the land in that year produced much grain. That year was the forty-fifth jubilee, the beginning of the eighth jubilee.

And Joseph took the fifth part of the harvest and brought it to the king. And the four parts were set aside for seed and for food. And to this day, Joseph has established this ordinance for the people of Egypt.

And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years. And all the years of his life were three jubilee years, which is three hundred forty-seven years. In the forty-fifth jubilee, he died in the eighth year of the jubilee.
And Jacob, before he died, blessed his children. He spoke concerning all that they would encounter in the land of Egypt, and in the latter days, he prophesied to them, and he blessed them.

And he gave Joseph two portions in the land, as his father had given him. And in the land of Canaan, he received a burial place beside his father Abraham. This is the burial place in the land of Canaan, where he was buried in the tomb of his fathers, and his books and the books of his fathers were preserved for his children until this day, to instruct them and to bless them.

And it came to pass after the death of Jacob, that the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great multitude. And brother loved brother, and neighbor helped neighbor, and all were united in heart.

And Joseph, during all the years of his life, was greatly esteemed in the land, for all the children of Israel were honored by the Egyptians. And after the death of his father Jacob, Joseph was not without care during all the days of his life; he did not suffer any evil.

And Joseph was a man of one hundred years when he died; he had lived in the land of Canaan for thirty-seven years, and had served for ten years, and had been in prison for three years; he had been under the king for eighty years, ruling over all the land of Egypt. And he died, and all his brothers died. And that generation also passed away.

And in the days when they were departing from Egypt, they commanded the children of Israel to take the bones of Joseph with them, lest they should die in the land of Canaan, as the Egyptians had made them to swear. And the king of Canaan, while dwelling in a land called Assur, was in conflict with the king of Egypt, and thus they were troubled.

Even unto the gate of Hermon did the Egyptians pursue; and there arose another king in Egypt who ruled, and they entered in; and they were more numerous than he, and they returned to the land of Canaan; and the gates of Egypt were shut; and there was no one who could go out or enter in.
And Joseph died in the forty-seventh jubilee in the second year of the second sabbath. And they buried him in the land of Egypt; and after him all his brothers died.
In the forty-seventh jubilee in the second sabbath in the second year, the king of Egypt went out to battle against the king of Canaan.
And the children of Israel, apart from Joseph, buried all the sons of Jacob in the wilderness, upon the mountain where there was no shelter.
And many people returned to Egypt; and among them few remained in Hebron; and your father remained with them.
The king of Canaan was victorious over the king of Egypt.

And the Egyptians said unto them, “Behold, the children of Israel are among us; let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass that when there is a war, they join our enemies and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.”

And they afflicted them with hard service, and they made their overseers to oppress them; they commanded them also. And for Pharaoh, they made strong taskmasters over them, to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh the treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses. But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And the Egyptians were in dread of the children of Israel.

In the forty-seventh year, in the seventh month, your father came from Canaan; in the forty-eighth year, in the third month, you were born; this was in a time of affliction upon the children of Israel.
And Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, commanded that every male child born to them should be cast into the river, thus he issued a decree against them.

And you remained until seven months, while they cast their children away. And your mother hid you for three months. And she did so for her, and made for you an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein, and laid it in the flags by the river's brink. And she remained there for seven days, and your mother came to nurse you by night, and your sister Miriam watched over you by day from afar.

And in those days, the son of Pharaoh was taken out to bathe in the river. And when she saw you, she commanded her maidservants to bring you to her. And she brought you to herself; and she raised you up.
Your sister said, “From among the Hebrews, who is this child that you are nursing, a woman of the Moabites?” And she called your mother, Jochebed; and she gave you her milk; and she nursed you.
After this, when you were weaned, you were brought to the house of Pharaoh. And you became his son. And your father taught you the book of the Hebrews.

And after you had completed three years, you were brought into the palace, and you dwelt in the palace for three years until the time you went out. And you saw your friend, the Hebrew, who was of the children of Israel, as he was being beaten by the Egyptian; and you killed him and buried him in the sand.

And on the second day, as you went out among the children of Israel, you found two men fighting. And you said to the one who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your brother?” And he answered, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?”
And when you heard this matter, you fled and escaped.

In the fortieth year, in the third month, in the sixth year, you went there; and you dwelt six months in one year. And in the seventh month, in the second year, you returned to Egypt; and this is the fiftieth year.

You know what was spoken to you on Mount Sinai; and when you returned to Egypt, on the way, on the day of the feast, the master of the feast asked you what you were to do. And he said, “Indeed, it is not so that you should be harmed.”

And concerning the Egyptians, you acted with cunning and judgment, and when you were sent, did you not save the Egyptians from your hand? And I have delivered you; and in Egypt, upon Pharaoh and upon all his household, upon all the servants and upon the people, you acted truly as you were sent, performing wonders and miracles.

And the Lord, concerning Israel, acted with great cunning against them. And by blood and by the blood of the lamb, by the small and by the great, by the evil and by the good, He utterly destroyed them.

And He destroyed their cattle by death and hail; and He consumed their harvests in all of this. And He destroyed the remnant that remained after the hail with a consuming locust. In darkness, both man and beast, and in all their idols, the Lord did this in secret. And He plagued them with fire; without doing anything, all was sent into Your hand.

You did speak to the king of Egypt before all his servants and before the people. All was done according to Your word. The great and wicked ten plagues came upon Egypt, that they might return to Israel in secret. And the Lord did all for Israel. By violence, as they had sold them, He returned to them in secret, as He had promised to Abraham.

The ruler was to be troubled before You, and he was to be cast down by Pharaoh's hand, and the Egyptians were to help him in their distress. They were also to be troubled. Before You, they were to do evil deeds. Before You, they were to do evil deeds, that they might be cast away. Yet poverty was to be done by their hand, and we did not permit them. And the Lord destroyed them with a wicked plague; even one miracle, though they did nothing, was made to trouble them.

The Egyptians, with all their armies, with their horses and their chariots, in Egypt, all the armies were to follow behind You until they were drowned, and to the Egyptians until they were heard, and the ruler was not to be spared by any miracle or wonder.
And I stood between you and the Egyptians, in the midst of Israel. And I delivered Israel from your hand and from the hand of his army.

And the Lord made them as dry land in the midst of the sea. And He led Israel, that all the Egyptians might follow them, and the children of Israel were cast into the sea as if they were thrown away, our God, the Lord, cast them beneath the waters. Ten times He made them to be troubled. Because they were cast among the children of Israel, a single child was to be thrown away among three hundred thousand soldiers.
On the fourteenth day and on the fifteenth day, on the sixteenth day and on the seventeenth day, on the eighteenth day, the ruler was to be troubled behind the children of Israel.

But on the nineteenth day, the Egyptians were to be troubled, that the children of Israel might follow them, and they were to be troubled. And their hearts were hardened, and they were strengthened; that they might be destroyed, the Egyptians were to be cast into the sea, that they might be cast down before our God, the Lord.

From the Egyptians, their garments and their money, the goods of silver, the goods of gold, and all their goods were to be taken on the day they were asked, that the children of Israel might not be cast away; and because of the violence they had done, they were to be made to suffer on the fourteenth day. The children of Israel were not to be sent away empty from Egypt.

The first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, while it was still evening, you shall eat it; and on the fifteenth day of the month, at the time when the sun is to set, you shall eat it at night, for the Lord commanded you concerning the Passover; this night is the beginning of the feast; it is the beginning of the Passover.

And you shall observe the Passover in the land of Egypt, and you shall eat it; for the Lord shall pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when He seeth the blood upon the lintel and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you; and He will destroy all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the firstborn of the maidservant that is behind the mill; and all the firstborn of beasts.

And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

And the Lord's host went forth as the Lord commanded, and they did all that He commanded. Not one of the children of Israel was left behind; from the cattle to the man, even unto the dog, not one of them was spared, for the destruction was sent forth to smite all the firstborn of the land of Egypt.

And the destruction was very great in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead. But all the children of Israel were gathered together, eating the flesh of the Passover and drinking the wine, giving thanks to the Lord their God, and blessing Him. They were prepared to go forth from Egypt, having been delivered from great distress.
Thou shalt remember this day in all thy generations; from one generation to another, in every age of thy life, thou shalt observe it as a statute, once every year.

For it is an everlasting ordinance; from day to day, from month to month, it shall not be neglected. Every year, on the same day, in every generation, they shall celebrate it as a feast, for it is a commandment from the Lord to the children of Israel.

A man shall be clean, and on the day of the feast, he shall offer the sacrifice unto the Lord; and if he does not come to eat and drink before the Lord, he shall not present the Lord's offering in its time, and he shall perish from among his people. That man shall bear the iniquity of his own sin. The day is divided into two parts, one for light and the other for darkness; the first month on the fourteenth day in the evening, from the third part of the day until the third part of the night, the children of Israel shall observe the feast.

In the midst of the nights, the feast shall be celebrated according to the ordinance that the Lord hath commanded. It shall be at night, but not in the light of day; until the night of the evening, they shall eat.

They shall roast it with fire, and they shall not eat it raw, nor sodden at all with water; but roast it with fire, its head with its legs and with the purtenance thereof. And nothing of it shall remain until the morning; that which remaineth until the morning shall be burnt with fire.

Therefore, in its time, ye shall celebrate the Passover, as the Lord commanded the children of Israel. And let not any of you break a bone thereof. For it is the day of the feast, and it is a commanded day; therefore, it shall not be passed from one day to another, nor from month to month.
You shall also command the children of Israel, saying, "In their seasons, every year, on the appointed day, they shall observe the Passover at its appointed time."

The remembrance that is beloved shall come before the Lord. In all things, as it has been commanded, at the appointed time when they observe the feast, in that season, the offerings shall not be brought to destroy them.

From now on, let their eating not be outside the house of the Lord, but rather let them eat in the house of the Lord, and in the presence of all the tribes of Israel, at the appointed time. Every man who comes from the age of twenty years and above shall eat before the Lord in His house, for it is written thus, and it has been commanded.

When the children of Israel have entered into the land of Canaan, after they have settled, the house of the Lord, where He is to be worshipped, shall be built in Jerusalem, until it is completed, and they shall gather together in one place on the earth to worship the Lord.
And let them also be those who observe the feast of Passover in the house of the Lord. Year by year, let them be present before the Lord.

Upon the land of the nations, in the name of the Lord, on the day when the house of the Lord is built, they shall go there, and at the setting of the sun, in the third part of the day, they shall observe the Passover; they shall sprinkle the blood around the altar; and the fat shall be placed upon the fire of the altar. And the flesh shall be eaten before the Lord at the entrance of the house of the Lord, roasted with fire.

It is in the house of the Lord that it shall be done; if not, it shall not be done in the city or in their region, for they cannot observe the Passover in their own cities; and they shall not depart from following the Lord.

And you, Moses, shall observe the ordinance of the Passover, year by year, day by day, as it has been commanded you, that in the feast they may eat unleavened bread for seven days; from the time you went out of Egypt until you come to the wilderness of Sur, this feast has been established for you, and at the shore of the sea, it has been completed, and the sacrifices shall be offered daily upon the altar of the Lord.

After this ordinance, on the day that is counted in the wilderness of Sin, I tell you, this wilderness is between Sin and Elom. And the land of the earth shall be counted in the wilderness of Sin. In the years of the jubilee, the years that are counted, I tell you, shall not be counted until you enter the land you are to possess. And upon her, in their dwelling, the land shall give rest. They shall know the year of jubilee.

Therefore, in the years that are counted, I have established the jubilee for you. From the time Adam was created until this day, there have been forty-nine jubilee years and one jubilee year from two years. To the west, until you enter the land of inheritance, the command of the Lord has not yet been known for forty years. Israel shall pass through the wilderness, from the wickedness, from the iniquity, from the transgression, from the sin, and from all error until they are cleansed, many jubilee years shall pass.

And upon the earth, it shall be desolate; from henceforth, there shall be none to dwell therein, nor shall any evil thing be found therein. And the earth shall be delivered from that day until the end of time.
Behold, I have written unto thee the ordinance of the sabbaths. I have written unto thee the judgment of the ordinance. In the six days, thou shalt do thy work.

The seventh day, however, is the day which the Lord your God has commanded you to rest from creation; you and your children, your male and female servants, and all your cattle, and even the stranger who dwells among you, shall not do any work. For on that day, anyone who does any work shall die. Whoever does work on this day, whether he be a man who meets with his wife, or one who goes to work, or one who engages in conversation, that man shall surely die.
Every man who sells or exchanges, and every man who draws water, and every man who has not prepared on the sixth day, whether from his dwelling or from his house, shall surely die.

On the sixth day, prepare what you shall prepare, and keep it holy, and on this day, cease from all your work. But on the day of the feast which you shall observe, give thanks to the Lord your God, and do no work on the sabbath day. It is a holy day; in their time, this day is a holy day for all Israel.

On this day of the feast, you shall rest and keep it holy before the Lord, and on every day and at every season, you shall offer your offerings, and your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings, except for any work that a man may do. This is the great honor that the Lord has given to Israel, and you shall honor it.

In your God, the Lord, in the house of the Lord, on the sabbath day, this work alone shall be done. To atone for the sins of the children of Israel, you shall bring your offerings before the Lord, day by day, as a reminder. As it has been commanded, so shall it be done for all generations, day by day.

Every man who works, and every man who walks, and every man who plows, whether in his house or in any place, and every man who kindles a fire, and every man who strikes an animal, and every man who sails upon the sea, shall die.

Every man who kills any creature, whether it be beast or fowl, whether it be a large beast or a bird, or a fish, or any man who slaughters, shall die. On the sabbath day, let him not kindle a fire, and whoever transgresses this ordinance and does any of these works on the sabbath day, that man shall die.

I shall write unto you the ordinances of the feast and of the day, as it has been commanded to me by the hand of the one who sent me from heaven, that the earth may rest as it has been commanded, that the children of Israel may observe the feast, and every man who works shall die.
